- *What stays free forever* (table stakes for a playable first impression):
  - Daily link puzzle.
  - At least one Combine theme at endless scope.
  - Item pages and bowtie explore.

**Pricing anchors:**
- One-off: $5 / $10 / $15 / $20 — small enough to be an impulse, large enough to feel one-time.
- Family/gift option (one payment unlocks for a shared account or multiple handles).

**Infrastructure notes:**
- Stripe is already in the planned stack (CLAUDE.md).
- Entitlement checks must be server-side (hard rule).
- Need an `entitlements` table keyed by user id, with status + source + purchased_at.
- UI can hint what's gated, but never ship gated data to the client.

**Risks / things to decide:**
- Is this child-friendly? Kids 8–12 are a plausible audience; one-off payment avoids subscription traps but may need adult-controlled purchase flow.
- Refund policy (digital one-off is usually no-refund, but be humane for mispurchases).
- Regional pricing — Stripe supports it; decide if we bother.
- Before shipping: confirm with user (per CLAUDE.md: "Ask before changing pricing").

**Not in scope yet:**
- Ads (ruled out by free-to-play + one-off framing).
- Subscriptions.
- In-run cosmetics or paid helpers (keep the game's integrity clean).

**Next step:** user picks the free/paid split, then this becomes concrete implementation tasks (entitlements table, Stripe wiring, UI gating, purchase flow).

title: Combine collection: reflect admin item changes (deprecation/removal) with notes
body:
When admins edit, deprecate, or remove items, players' collections (`combine_discoveries`) should reflect those changes cleanly — and the player should get a note when something they collected changes meaningfully.

**Scenarios to handle:**

1. **Item removed / deprecated** (admin deletes or sets `status` away from `live`):
   - Discovery row exists but the item no longer renders.
   - Options:
     - **Soft-retire:** keep the row, render it as "deprecated" with a note ("No longer in Made Of — you discovered it before it was retired").
     - **Hide:** remove from the active collection view, keep in a "legacy" section.
     - **Hard-delete:** cascade erase. Bad — loses player progress. Current `ON DELETE CASCADE` on `combine_discoveries.itemId` makes this the default; see existing memory [Seed wipes Combine discoveries].
   - Recommendation: soft-retire with a visible note. Needs schema: either drop the cascade and add a `retired_at` on the discovery row, or keep an archival snapshot (name, pictogram, tier) alongside the item id.

2. **Item renamed / pictogram changed:**
   - The collection updates naturally (reads from `items`).
   - If the change is substantial (name is meaningfully different), optionally surface a "This item was updated" note on the collection card.

3. **Item moved out of a theme:**
   - Discovery stays (scope is `endless` or `daily`, not per-theme). No action needed except not re-offering it in that theme.

4. **Item split / merged** (future):
   - Split: one discovery becomes two? Flag for admin review rather than auto-split.
   - Merge: two discoveries collapse into one — add a note on the survivor.

**What "with a note" means:**
- On the collection card, a small badge: "Updated" / "Retired" / "Merged."
- Tap → short modal: what changed, when, and (if applicable) the new item it points to.
- Don't spam: only notes for meaningful changes, not every pictogram touch-up.

**Admin side:**
- When deleting/deprecating a live item, the admin UI should warn how many user discoveries point to it.
- Offer options at delete-time: retire-with-note, redirect-to-another-item, or hard-delete (dangerous, confirm).

**Schema implications:**
- Likely want to drop `ON DELETE CASCADE` on `combine_discoveries.itemId` (per existing memory, this was already a source of pain).
- Add nullable fields: `retired_at`, `redirected_to_item_id`, `change_note`.

**Related:**
- [Seed wipes Combine discoveries](memory) — same root cause (cascade on itemId).
- T-0007 (bulk upload draft/review flow) — adjacent "lifecycle of items" concern.
- T-0034 (discovery notifications) — same surface, same "card" treatment.

**Open:**
- Do retired items still count toward partial-completion milestones (T-0008)? Probably yes for everything you earned before retirement, so the milestone doesn't regress.
- Audit trail: do we need an immutable log of every discovery change for support purposes?

title: Content: add "chemical salt" (NaCl) as distinct item from natural salt
body:
We currently only have **natural salt** (geologic/biological source — seawater, rock salt). Add **chemical salt** as a separate item — synthesised NaCl from elements — because their provenance differs.

Shape:
- New item: "chemical salt" (or "synthetic salt" / "NaCl" — pick a name consistent with how other chem items are named).
- Recipe: `Na + Cl → chemical salt`.
- Provenance chain traces back through elemental sodium and chlorine → stars → big bang.
- Natural salt keeps its existing links (seawater `s`, rock `s`, etc.) — no changes.
- Decide theme membership (Everyday? Everything? neither?) and tier.

Why distinct items, not one:
- A single "salt" item would need multi-parent provenance that mixes two totally different origin stories — Made Of's whole point is that the chain is real and sourced. Two items keeps each chain honest.
- Downstream recipes (table salt in food, salt in chemistry) may legitimately point to one source or the other.

Open:
- Should bowtie/explore link them visually as "siblings" / "see also"?
- Are there other items with the same split problem worth auditing in one pass (e.g., water — tap vs distilled? sugar — cane vs synthetic?)? Likely yes, but out of scope for this task — flag follow-up if found.

Related: T-0033 (this was the test case for the mobile recipe editor).

title: Item page bugs: dedupe "Made from" ingredients; fix empty black button under "First appeared"
body:
Two visible bugs on the item page (seen on `nucleotides`):

**1. Duplicate ingredients in "Made from".**
- The list shows carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus, carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus — each appears twice.
- Likely cause: nucleotides have multiple recipes (each nucleobase has its own recipe that shares the same ingredients), and the "Made from" view is unioning recipe-scoped `f` links without deduping by target item.
- Fix: dedupe by target item id in the "Made from" roll-up. Keep the per-recipe view separate if we need it elsewhere.
- Audit: check other items with multiple recipes for the same symptom (water, salt, common molecules).

**2. Empty black button under "First appeared / Date not yet known".**
- A large dark rectangle renders with no label, no icon, no obvious action.
- Likely: a button or chip that's missing its text/icon when the data is absent (e.g., "date not yet known" clears the content but the button shell stays).
- Fix: hide the button entirely when there's no first-appeared date; or render a de-emphasized "Add a date" link for admins only.

Where to look:
- "Made from" roll-up: likely in the item page's bowtie or ingredient-list component.
- Empty button: the "First appeared" row near the item header.

Open:
- The duplication may actually be *recipe-aware* data (two recipes = two sets of inputs), in which case the fix is to group them by recipe with a recipe header. Confirm the intended design before deduping blindly.

title: Combine: add spacing between "Keep playing" and "Wipe" helper buttons
body:
"Keep playing" and "Wipe" buttons sit flush against each other — no gap between them. Easy misclick, especially on mobile.

**Context:** "Wipe" is a **helper**, not a progress-wipe — it clears the current board/tray within a run. So the risk is wasting a helper charge, not losing a collection.

Fix:
- Add a visible gap (e.g., `gap-3` / 12–16px) between the two buttons.
- Minor: give Wipe a slightly distinct visual so the two actions don't read as one control, but no confirm dialog needed (it's just a helper).

Where: Combine in-run UI where helpers live (likely the helper tray near the board).

Open:
- While we're here, audit other helper buttons for spacing consistency (hint, move, reroll, etc.) so they all follow the same gap rule.

comments.body: Blocked on T-0045's ButtonGroup component work. The "Wipe / Keep playing" ConfirmDialog is one of the call sites being migrated to the new primitive (which bakes in the gap). T-0043 closes when T-0045 lands — no separate fix.

title: Combine: confirmation dialog before Wipe helper fires
body:
The Wipe helper clears the board/tray and consumes a helper charge. Right now it's a one-tap action, so a misclick wastes the charge and the board state.

Add a confirm dialog:
- "Wipe the board? This uses 1 helper and can't be undone."
- Primary: "Wipe" (destructive styling).
- Secondary: "Cancel."

Keep the dialog lightweight — a small modal or bottom-sheet on mobile, not a full-screen takeover.

Options to consider so the confirm doesn't become friction for intentional users:
- "Don't ask again this run" checkbox — honours the player's choice without a persistent setting.
- Or: no confirm on first use in a run, but confirm if remaining helpers are few (≤ 1).

Related:
- T-0043 (button spacing) — addresses misclick from the layout side; this addresses it from the action side. Ship both.
- T-0029 (move helper interaction) — part of the broader helper-UX pass.

title: Audit horizontal button rows app-wide: establish a gap primitive so this stops recurring
body:
**Immediate:** "Share" and "Play again" buttons in the "Board full" dialog sit flush against each other, same symptom as T-0043 (Keep playing / Wipe).

**Root cause (suspected):** horizontal button rows in the codebase aren't consistently using a `gap`. It's probably multiple ad-hoc flex rows per surface, each written without a shared primitive, so every new dialog ships the bug fresh.

**Fix at two levels:**

1. **Fix the "Board full" dialog now** — add gap between Share and Play again.

2. **Establish a shared button-row primitive** so this stops happening:
   - A single `<ButtonRow>` (or CSS class) that any horizontal set of buttons passes through.
   - Default gap (12–16px), default wrap behaviour, default stretch/equal-width on mobile.
   - Lint rule / grep guard: any `flex` + button-pair that isn't using the primitive gets flagged in review.
   - Pairs well with the CSS modules migration (T-0002) and tile-styling centralization (T-0006) — same "centralize or it drifts" problem.

3. **Audit sweep** — grep for flex rows with multiple buttons across:
   - Combine: board-full dialog, keep-playing/wipe helper area (T-0043), game-over, Fast mode game-over.
   - Craft: result / share screens.
   - Link: daily puzzle result dialog, share.
   - Item page: any action rows.
   - Admin: toolbar rows on `/admin/tree`, modal footers.

**Open:**
- On mobile, horizontal button rows often want to stack vertically with more spacing — the primitive should handle the breakpoint, not every caller.
- Share buttons often have different visual weight than Play again — primitive should let callers mark primary/secondary without losing the gap.

comments.body:
## Investigation (no code changes)

### Root cause confirmed

`.row2` has **no base rule** in `src/app/globals.css`. It only gets `display:flex; gap:...` when scoped to a parent class:

- `.aev .row2` — about page config grid (line 348, gap 10px)
- `.cblastchance-sheet .row2` — Last Chance sheet (line 745, gap 10px)
- `.cbover .row2, .cbinfo .row2` — DetailCard + the deprecated `.cbover` (line 1401, gap 12px)

Any JSX that drops `<div className="row2">` into a `ResponsiveSheet` **without** one of those scope classes renders with no `display:flex`, no gap — just a bare block container stacking buttons. That's the drift.

### Bugged surfaces today

1. **`GameOverCard.tsx:137`** — `ResponsiveSheet` has no `className` prop; the `.row2` wrapping Share/Play again has no styling. This *is* the "Board full" dialog bug the task opened with.
2. **`ConfirmDialog.tsx:46`** — also uses a bare `ResponsiveSheet`; `.row2` has no styling. Affects the "Wipe the board?" confirmation (T-0043's reported symptom) and any other confirm dialog (e.g., about page).

### Surfaces that work today (just by luck of scope)

- `DetailCard` passes `className="cbinfo"` → `.cbinfo .row2` kicks in.
- `CombineBoard` Last Chance sheet passes `className="cblastchance-sheet"` → scoped rule kicks in.
- About page uses `.aev .row2` (grid variant, different shape).

### Wider audit

The exploration agent found **13 distinct button-row class names** (`.row`, `.row2`, `.cbresultsrow`, `.cbrestartrow`, `.cbonboard-actions`, `.pkrow`, `.chainrow`, `.lrow`, `.pbtns`, `.cbhelp`, `.tierrow`, `.tree-row-actions-inline`, `.tree-recipe-actions-inline`) + 2 inline-style-only patterns. All **other** rows have gap set; only `.row2` is the broken primitive (because its "default" is implicit and missing).

Agent initially reported all rows OK because it checked each row class in isolation. The actual bug surfaces only when you combine a bare `ResponsiveSheet` + `.row2` — cross-file dependency.

### Recommended fix (two-step, scoped to T-0045 + T-0043)

1. **Immediate (fixes T-0043 and T-0045's "Board full" symptom):** add a base `.row2{display:flex;gap:12px;width:100%;margin-top:4px}` rule in globals.css. Scoped variants (`.cblastchance-sheet .row2`, `.aev .row2`) stay for their size/layout overrides but inherit gap correctly. Tiny blast radius: one new CSS block, zero JSX changes, all six current `.row2` call sites validate.

2. **Follow-up / drift prevention (bigger):** collapse `.row`, `.row2`, `.cbresultsrow`, `.cbrestartrow` into a single `.btnrow` primitive with modifiers (`btnrow-tight` for 8px, `btnrow-spaced` for 12px, `btnrow-stack@sm` for mobile stacking). Migrate the ~13 call sites. The in-codebase idiom is already "primitive + modifier" (see `.cbchip` from T-0053). That's the right final shape, but it's a separate refactor task — this ticket can close on step 1.

### Follow-up task proposal

If you want step 2, I can file it as its own task that depends on T-0045. The investigation notes above should be enough to scope it.

### Related

- T-0043: same root cause, same one-line CSS fix resolves it.
- T-0053: landed the `.cbchip` primitive — identical "centralize to stop drift" pattern, same shape we'd want for button rows.
- T-0002 (CSS modules) / T-0006 (tile primitive): same umbrella.

Landed: `` component + full migration of action-button rows. New primitive: - `src/components/common/ButtonGroup.tsx` — React component with `size` (`tight`/`default`/`spaced`), `align` (`stretch`/`start`/`end`/`center`), `stack` (`never`/`mobile`/`always`), `className`/`style`/`as` passthroughs. - `src/app/globals.css:411-432` — `.btngroup` base + modifier classes. Default is dialog-action flavour: 12px gap, 4px top margin, equal-width stretched children, tall (44px) `.cbh` targets. Migrations (10 call sites): - `src/components/common/ConfirmDialog.tsx` — Cancel/Confirm (fixes T-0043 "Wipe / Keep playing"). - `src/components/combine/board-parts/overlays/GameOverCard.tsx` — Share/Play again (fixes T-0045 "Board full" symptom). - `src/components/combine/board-parts/overlays/DetailCard.tsx` — Explore/Back. - `src/components/combine/board-parts/overlays/ThemeMenu.tsx` — Keep playing/Restart. - `src/components/combine/CombineBoard.tsx` — Last Chance sheet + the fixed-position Results/Share floating bar (keeps `.cbresultsrow` as positioning-only wrapper). - `src/components/combine/board-parts/onboarding.tsx` — Skip/Replay/Next trio. - `src/components/craft/CraftBoard.tsx` — Play again/New target on the win screen. - `src/app/not-found.tsx` — 404 mode-picker row. Deletions (stale CSS): - `.cbover .row2, .cbinfo .row2` + their `.cbh` child rule. - `.cblastchance-sheet .row2` + its `.cbh` child rule. - `.cbrestartrow`. - Trimmed `.cbonboard-actions` down to `margin-top:6px` (layout now from ButtonGroup). - Trimmed `.cbresultsrow` to positioning-only (flex/gap gone, ButtonGroup handles layout). Not migrated (deliberate): - `.aev .row2` on the about page — same class name, but it's a grid layout, not a button row. Left alone. - `.row` usages in CraftBoard pause/hint row and LinkBoard copy-result row — those mix buttons with status `

` / ``, not pure button groups. - `.cbhelp`, `.pbtns`, `.tierrow`, `.chainrow`, `.lrow`, `.howto-glyph .row`, `.tree-*-actions-inline` — not action rows; different jobs (helper tray, form status, layout grids, admin table toolbars). Verification: - `npm run typecheck` clean. - `grep -rn 'cbrestartrow\|cblastchance-sheet .row2' src` → no results. - `npm test` — 2 pre-existing failures in `src/combine/__tests__/engine.test.ts` unrelated to this change (they fail on the uncommitted `engine.ts` edits in the working tree from a prior session). T-0043 is unblocked by this landing — the Wipe/Keep playing ConfirmDialog is one of the migrated sites and now has the 12px gap baked in. Closing T-0043 alongside.

title: Combine theme dialog: make "Restart" scope explicit (which mode × theme)
body:
In the Combine theme dialog, there are **Endless** and **Fast** mode choices for each theme, but a single **"Restart everything"** button. It's unclear which (mode × theme) the restart actually affects — one mode? One theme? All combinations?

Fix options (pick one, probably the first):

1. **Per-button restart icon** colocated with each (mode, theme) tile.
   - Each theme × mode card gets a small ↻ icon button in a corner.
   - Tap → confirms "Restart Endless · Everyday?" so the scope is unambiguous.
   - No big "Restart everything" at the bottom at all.

2. **Rename the button to name the target.**
   - "Restart Endless · Everyday" / "Restart Fast · Everything" — whatever's currently selected.
   - Still one button, but it reads its scope from the current selection.

3. **Explicit scope dropdown** next to Restart.
   - "Restart [this mode + theme ▾]" with options for broader scopes if we want them.
   - Overkill for the common case.

Recommendation: **#1**. Per-card restart is instantly clear and matches how players mentally model "this theme's run."

Also:
- Confirm dialog on restart should spell out what's cleared — in-progress run? collection (endless scope is lifetime — that would be destructive)? Just the current session?
- If "Restart" is wiping collection progress (endless scope), that needs a strong confirm with the exact words.
- If it's just "abandon current run and start fresh," that's low-risk — one-tap with a brief undo toast might be enough.

Open:
- What does "Restart everything" currently do in code? Audit before changing the UI so we know what we're renaming.
- Does the daily scope have its own restart? Probably not (daily is daily), but confirm.

- On the expanded tile card (hover / tap-detail view), as a small badge beside the name. Same badge style already used on item pages (see nucleotides screenshot: `NATURAL` `SUBSTANCE` chips).
- Probably not on the base tile itself — tier color already encodes "where this sits in the hierarchy," and adding kind text would clutter the pictogram tile.

Why it's useful:
- Helps players learn the taxonomy without reading long descriptions.
- Pairs nicely with the kind-grouped collection view (referenced in T-0008) — if players see "SUBSTANCE" on cards, the "all substances" milestone makes immediate sense.

- Multi-kind items? If an item can have more than one kind, show all or just primary? (Nucleotides example shows two.)

title: Tile card: fix black pictograms and misplaced "+" in recipe-input row
body:
Two small-but-visible bugs on the tile card's recipe-input row:

**1. Pictograms render black.**
- Inside the ingredient chips on the tile card, pictograms are rendering as a solid black fill instead of the usual tier-coloured tile + ink stroke used everywhere else.
- Likely cause: a wrong CSS variable, missing `currentColor` fill, or the chip is using a stripped-down pictogram component that skips the fill layer.
- Expected: same look as pictograms on the board / Hold tray / item page.

**2. The `+` sits inside the first chip instead of between chips.**
- Current: `[◆ Water +] [◇ Oxygen]` — the `+` is contained within the left chip's border.
- Expected: `[◆ Water] + [◇ Oxygen]` — the `+` is a standalone separator between chips.
- Likely cause: the `+` is rendered as a trailing character inside the chip's content rather than as a sibling node in the row.

Fix:
- Move the `+` out of the chip component. Render the row as: `chip`, `separator ("+")`, `chip`, … so the `+` can't accidentally live inside any chip's border.
- Make sure the pictogram inside each chip uses the shared Tile/pictogram rendering path (ties into T-0006 — centralize tile styling).

Related:
- T-0006 (centralize tile styling across surfaces).
- T-0047 (end-screen tile layout) — same "chips should match the shared tile look" theme.

Open:
- Share preview might embed the same chip component — re-check the share image after the fix.

Left alone — they're different, denser layouts and were not called out by the user. If T-0006 (shared tile styling) lands, revisit as part of that sweep. **Follow-ups** - Shared tile styling (T-0006) is the long-term fix; this is the narrow DetailCard patch. - Share preview uses a server-rendered OG card, not this chip component — no regression risk there. **Verification** - `npm run typecheck` clean. - Visual check against the directory-page screenshot the user shared recommended before close.

title: Combine: age progression counts every recipe execution, not unique discoveries (bug)
body:
**Confirmed bug.** Age progression increments on every successful combine, not on unique first-time discoveries at the current age's band.

**Evidence (from a code audit):**

- **`src/combine/engine.ts:481`** — the increment:
  ```ts
  if (recipe.band === state.age + 1 && mult === 1) state.ageMade++;
  ```
  No check against `state.found` — so duplicates count.

- **`src/combine/engine.ts:528, 542`** — the age-up comparison:
  ```ts
  if (state.age < totalAges - 1 && state.ageMade >= ageNeed(state.age, bundle))
  ```

- **`src/combine/engine.ts:293–300`** — the documented intent of `ageNeed`:
  > "Unique discoveries at the current age's band needed to leave each age. Only first-time makes of items whose minimum band is `age + 1` count."
  The comment says unique; the implementation doesn't enforce it.

- **Adjacent state used correctly elsewhere:**
  - `state.found[]` (lines 466–468) already tracks unique item ids via `!state.found.includes(recipe.out)`.
  - `state.madeCounts[recipe.out]` (line 473) is the "repeat makes" counter — distinct from first-finds.

So the fix pattern already exists in the same file for discovery tracking; it just isn't used for `ageMade`.

**Fix:**
- At line 481, only increment when the item is a first-time find at its band:
  ```ts
  if (recipe.band === state.age + 1 && mult === 1 && !state.found.includes(recipe.out))
    state.ageMade++;
  ```
  (Place this before line 466's `found.push`, or hoist the first-find check so both branches share it.)
- Add a unit test: make the same item twice at the current age → `ageMade` goes up by 1, not 2.

**Scope / impact:**
- This has been shipped, so historical runs scored under the lenient (buggier) rule. Decide:
  - (a) Leave historical `progress` rows alone, new rows use the fixed rule — leaderboards will have a soft reset at the fix date.
  - (b) Backfill nothing — data loss risk and we don't have the per-combine log to recompute.
  - Recommended: (a). Note the change in `append_changelog`.

**Related:**
- T-0030 (unique ages scoring bug) — adjacent "unique-vs-not" bug in a different counter. Worth looking at both together.
- T-0005 (serve age chains from server) — tangential, but if we're touching age logic, consider whether the fix has any implications there.
- The `2026-11 bug` note in `src/combine/data.ts` (band collapse when `numAges > uniqueLevels`) is a **separate** issue, not this one.

**Open:**
- Should Fast mode use the same fixed rule? Yes — same engine, same intent.
- Confirm the change doesn't make ages unreachable for small themes / Everyday (fewer unique band items means hitting `ageNeed` is harder). If so, lower `ageNeed` as part of the same change.

comments.body:
**Approach**

- **Fix:** hoist the first-find check so both the discovery branch and the age-progression increment share it. Concretely in `src/combine/engine.ts` around line 466:
  ```ts
  const first = state.mode !== "fast" && !state.found.includes(recipe.out);
  ```
  becomes two signals — the discovery gate (which must stay fast-mode-aware) and the unique-at-band gate for ageMade. Cleanest version: compute `const uniqueFind = !state.found.includes(recipe.out)` before the mutations, keep the `first` definition for discovery event, and change line 481 to:
  ```ts
  if (recipe.band === state.age + 1 && mult === 1 && uniqueFind) state.ageMade++;
  ```
  Order matters: must read `uniqueFind` BEFORE `state.found.push(recipe.out)` on line 468.

- **Fast mode:** Fast skips `found.push` entirely (see line 466 — gated on `state.mode !== "fast"`), so under the current implementation every craft in Fast is "not in found". If we naively use `!state.found.includes`, Fast would age up on dupes too (same bug just via a different path). **Decision:** Fast mode runs are short (2-part only, no bands) — need to verify Fast actually hits the age-up path at all. Looking at engine behavior now.

- **Test:** add to `tests/` — simulate: same single-band item crafted twice at age 0 → `state.ageMade === 1`. Also: two different band items → `ageMade === 2`.

- **Reachability sanity check:** inspect `ageNeed` for Everyday + Everything themes after the fix. If any band's `bandSize * UNLOCK_FRACTION` floors below `baselineNeed`, we're fine. If it climbs above the number of unique items in the band, ages become unreachable — would need a cap at `bandSize(age, bundle)`.

- **History:** No backfill. Note the soft leaderboard reset in changelog.

**Files I'll touch:**
- `src/combine/engine.ts` — the fix (and verify fast mode behavior)
- `tests/combine-engine.test.ts` (or nearest existing engine test) — new test cases

**Landed**

- **`src/combine/engine.ts:466-486`** — hoisted `uniqueFind = !state.found.includes(recipe.out)` above the mutations; gated `state.ageMade++` on `(state.mode === "fast" || uniqueFind)`. Updated the inline comment block to explain the new contract.
- **`src/combine/__tests__/engine.test.ts`** — added `describe("ageMade counts only unique on-band first-finds (T-0051)")` with 3 cases:
  - re-making the same on-band item doesn't bump `ageMade`
  - two different on-band items each bump it
  - fast mode keeps counting repeats (its `ageMade` is just a termination signal, not real progression — Fast skips `found.push` so a naive `uniqueFind` check would make Fast runs never terminate via `ageMade`)

**Test results:** 84 passed / 2 failed in engine.test.ts. The 2 failures are pre-existing hold-zone tests that fail on `main` before my change (confirmed via `git stash`) — unrelated.

**Typecheck:** clean. Full suite: 293 passed / 2 failed (same pre-existing failures).

**Didn't do:**
- No `progress` backfill — noted the soft leaderboard reset in changelog.
- Didn't lower `ageNeed`: reachability sanity check — `ageNeed = max(baselineNeed(age), round(bandSize * 0.4))` is always `<= bandSize` for the realistic case (0.4 ≤ 1), and `baselineNeed(age) = 7 + 2*age` is unlikely to exceed `bandSize` for Everything's authored ages. Everyday has fewer items per band but still comfortably above 7 for age 0. If a small theme bumps this later, we'll see it as an unreachable-age bug and can cap at `bandSize(age, bundle)` in `ageNeed`.
- The 2 pre-existing hold-zone failures: tracked separately, not T-0051 scope.

title: Audio: dies on tab switch / refresh and won't resume
body:
Audio dies on tab switch / refresh and won't resume. Different from T-0032 (which proposed *intentionally* pausing on visibilitychange) — here the pause-on-hide path exists but the resume path is broken.

**Repro:**
- Leave tab → music fades out and audio context is suspended
- Return to tab → music does not resume
- Sometimes same thing happens after refresh

**Audio architecture (for reference):**
- Web Audio API, no Howler/Tone
- `src/combine/audio/core.ts` — AudioContext singleton (`ensureContext`), master/compressor/reverb buses, `suspendAudio()`, `silence()`
- `src/combine/audio/music.ts` — generative scheduler (piano, chimes, drift); `startMusic()` calls `core.ctx.resume()` at line ~195
- `src/combine/audio/sfx.ts` — SFX dispatcher
- `src/components/combine/CombineBoard.tsx` — integration; state `{ music, sfx, vol }` persisted to `madeof:music` / `madeof:sfx` / `madeof:vol` in localStorage
- Context is unlocked on first `pointerdown` via `ensureContext()` (CombineBoard.tsx:298–312)

**Visibility handling today (CombineBoard.tsx:334–347):**
- `visibilitychange` → hidden: `fadeOutMusic()` then `suspendAudio()`
- `visibilitychange` → visible: if `sound.music !== 'off' && hasContext()` → `startMusic(...)`
- `pagehide` → `silence()`

**Likely root causes:**
1. On return, `startMusic()` calls `ctx.resume()`, but the generative scheduler's oscillators were disconnected/stopped during fade+suspend — resume doesn't restart the scheduler, so audio graph is silent even once context is running.
2. The visibility effect's dep array (`[sound, state.age]`) may not re-fire the branch cleanly across hide→show without a state change.
3. On refresh, the user-gesture unlock listener may not re-arm reliably, so `ensureContext()` never runs and music can't start at all.

**Scope:**
- Make visible-handler reliably resume: call `core.ctx.resume()` *and* restart the scheduler from scratch (not rely on it still being wired).
- Verify gesture-unlock listener re-arms after refresh.
- Confirm `fadeOutMusic` cleans up scheduler state so `startMusic` can cold-start without leaks.

comments.body:
**Root cause (confirmed by reading the code, not guessed):**

The visibility effect at `src/components/combine/CombineBoard.tsx:318` captured `suspendTimer` as a `let` local to each effect run. Flow of the bug:

1. Tab hides → `silence()` calls `fadeOutMusic()` (clears scheduler, ramps musicBus gain to 0) then `setTimeout(suspendAudio, fade+20ms)`.
2. While the tab is hidden, `state.age` or `sound` changes → the effect's dep array fires → cleanup runs, old handlers detach, new effect run starts with a fresh `suspendTimer = null` closure. The pending `setTimeout` from the previous run is now orphaned and the new `onVis` closure can't see it.
3. Tab becomes visible → new `onVis` checks its own (null) `suspendTimer`, skips the cancel, calls `startMusic()` which does `ctx.resume()` and restarts the scheduler.
4. Moments later the orphaned `setTimeout` fires `suspendAudio(core)` → context goes back to suspended. Scheduler keeps ticking against a suspended context. Silent.

**Fix (`src/components/combine/CombineBoard.tsx:323`):**
- Lift the pending-suspend timer into `suspendTimerRef = useRef<number | null>(null)` so cancel-on-visible catches the pending timer across effect re-runs.
- Removed the `clearTimeout` from the effect's cleanup — if the component unmounts legitimately we still want the suspend to land, and we no longer need per-run cleanup now that the ref is shared.

**Audio-on by default (addresses T-0025):**
- `src/combine/storage.ts:48` — `SOUND_DEFAULT` now `{ music: "piano", sfx: true, vol: 80 }`.
- `src/components/combine/CombineBoard.tsx:281` — matched useState initial value so there's no "off" flash before `loadSound()` runs.
- Existing users' localStorage settings are preserved (loadSound only falls back to defaults when the key is absent).
- Browser autoplay rules still apply: the pointerdown listener at `:298` unlocks the context on first gesture, which is unchanged.

**Verification:**
- `npm run typecheck` clean.
- `npm run lint` clean (only pre-existing warnings, nothing new introduced).
- Not manually tested in browser yet — tab-switch repro needs a live dev server.

title: Combine reactions (👍/👎/report) — recipes + items
body:
Inline thumbs reactions on Combine recipes, deferred from T-0011. See parent for full spec.

Shape:
- `recipe_reactions` table (`recipe_id`, `user_id`, `value smallint` {-1, 1}, `reason text?`, `created_at`). Unique on `(recipe_id, user_id)` so a vote can flip.
- Hook into `DiscoveryToast` (`src/components/combine/board-parts/toasts.tsx:170`) — small 👍/👎 pair next to the recipe chip.
- `POST /api/combine/recipe-reactions` — auth required.
- Admin view: recipes sorted by net sentiment, filterable (likely folds into T-0035 admin analytics).

Depends on T-0011 landing first (so the admin feedback UI pattern is established).

comments.body:
## Approach

### Decisions (confirmed with user)

- **Vote key**: `recipe_id` (DB row). Simpler, matches parent spec, clean admin triage.
- **Surfaces**: `DiscoveryToast` + `DetailCard` + `CollectionBook` list rows. Replace the standalone "Report" button on DetailCard with a 3-button group (up / down / report).
- **Downvote flow**: quiet — vote records -1 immediately; a small "Tell us why?" chip appears after a downvote and opens the Report sheet prefilled when tapped. Not modal.
- **Icons**: inline SVGs matching pictogram line style (`stroke: var(--ink)`, 32×32 viewBox). No emoji anywhere.

### Resolving the recipe id

The client needs a `recipe_id` to vote on. Today the engine carries `inputSignature` (sorted ingredients) on `combine` events — not an id. Two options:

1. **Thread recipe ids through the engine events** — add `recipeId: string` to the `combine` + `discovery` events and to `howMade`. Requires changing engine state; small but touches tests.
2. **Client-side resolution** — given output + ingredient signature, look up the bundle recipe. `bundle.sameIngredients.get(sig)` filters to candidates, then pick the one with `.out === out`. Only works if the bundle carries recipe ids.

Right now `CombineRecipe` doesn't carry a recipe id (bundles are built from the graph snapshot). I'll add `id: string` to `CombineRecipe`, populate it from the snapshot's recipe rows, and expose it on the UI surfaces directly from `howMade`-matched / discovery-event-matched recipes. Option 2 effectively, but with the id available on the recipe itself.

### Schema (migration 0017)

```sql
CREATE TABLE recipe_reactions (
  recipe_id   UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES recipes(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  user_id     TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES "user"(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  value       SMALLINT NOT NULL CHECK (value IN (-1, 1)),
  reason      TEXT,
  created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  PRIMARY KEY (recipe_id, user_id)
);
CREATE INDEX recipe_reactions_recipe_idx ON recipe_reactions(recipe_id);
```

PK is `(recipe_id, user_id)` so votes flip on `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`.

### API

- `POST /api/combine/recipe-reactions` body `{recipeId, value: 1 | -1 | 0, reason?: string}`:
  - `value: 1 | -1` → upsert.
  - `value: 0` → delete (toggle-off semantics).
  - `reason` → updates the stored reason if present.
  - Auth required.
- `GET /api/combine/recipe-reactions?ids=a,b,c` → `{byId: Record<recipeId, {mine: -1|1|null, up: number, down: number}>}` for a batch of recipe ids. Only `mine` is strictly needed for the UI (toast / card); `up` / `down` aggregates are useful for admin surfacing later and for anti-abuse heuristics. Scope to signed-in users; unauth returns `mine: null` everywhere.

### Client-side hook

`useRecipeReactions(recipeIds: string[])`:
- On mount + ids change, fetch `/api/combine/recipe-reactions?ids=...` for the active ids.
- Returns `{reactions: Map<recipeId, {mine, up, down}>, vote(recipeId, value, reason?) }`.
- `vote` is optimistic: update local state immediately, POST in the background; roll back on error.
- Signed-out players: no fetch, `vote` is a no-op (buttons render as sign-in prompts? or just disabled with a tooltip — see UI).

### UI primitive

New `<ReactionButtons recipeId value onVote onReport />` component in `src/components/combine/board-parts/ReactionButtons.tsx`:
- Three buttons in a horizontal `ButtonGroup`:
  - Thumbs-up SVG (fill: var(--good) when `value === 1`, outline otherwise).
  - Thumbs-down SVG (fill: var(--bad) when `value === -1`, outline otherwise).
  - Flag/report SVG → opens Report sheet.
- After a downvote, render a muted chip below: `Tell us why?` → clicking sets a reason on the existing downvote and opens Report prefilled with `category: "recipe_wrong"` plus the recipe context. Dismissable.
- Signed-out: thumbs act as "sign in to react" (clicking routes to `/sign-in`), or disabled. Report stays functional.

### Wiring per surface

- **DiscoveryToast** (`toasts.tsx:145`): already takes `onReport`. Extend with `recipeId` + reactions lookup. Replace the standalone report button with `<ReactionButtons>`. The toast auto-dismisses after 4.6s — if the player has interacted with the buttons, cancel the dismiss timer (don't rip the UI out while they're reacting). Re-arm on blur.
- **DetailCard** (`DetailCard.tsx`): currently renders a standalone "Report" button. Each `recipeRows` entry has a signature — resolve to the recipe id via the bundle, and render `<ReactionButtons>` next to each row. The top-level "Report" button goes away (the per-row group replaces it for recipes; an item-level flag stays in the row2 button pair).
- **CollectionBook list rows** (`CollectionBook.tsx`): discoveries rows show recipe chips. Compact `<ReactionButtons variant="xs">` at the end of each recipe chip (just up/down for density; report is the DetailCard's responsibility on this surface to avoid clutter). Actually — user confirmed all three, so include report here too. Use the `xs` variant.

### Edge cases

- **Admin recipe row deleted/restructured**: `ON DELETE CASCADE` wipes votes for the deleted row. Fine — the vote is about that specific authoring, and if it's gone, so is the signal.
- **Rate limiting**: in-memory limiter already exists; add `recipe-reactions` to the list with a loose budget (30/min seems fine; this is cheap writes).
- **Duplicate/flip votes**: same user hitting ↑ then ↓ writes -1 (upsert). Hitting ↑ again when `value === 1` clears the vote (toggle semantics via `value: 0` → DELETE).

### Not in scope

- Admin triage view (folds into T-0035 per parent task).
- Showing vote counts on the player UI. Only the player's own vote is reflected. Public counts could reveal rough player taste which some players would game.
- Any batch undo / "remove all my reactions" surface.

### Files

- `drizzle/0017_*.sql`, `src/db/schema.ts` — recipe_reactions table
- `src/app/api/combine/recipe-reactions/route.ts` — GET + POST
- `src/combine/useRecipeReactions.ts` — client hook
- `src/components/combine/board-parts/ReactionButtons.tsx` — new primitive
- `src/components/combine/board-parts/toasts.tsx` — DiscoveryToast wiring
- `src/components/combine/board-parts/overlays/DetailCard.tsx` — per-row buttons
- `src/components/combine/board-parts/overlays/CollectionBook.tsx` — per-recipe-chip buttons
- `src/components/combine/CombineBoard.tsx` — thread hook + recipe id resolution
- `src/combine/types.ts` — add `id: string` to `CombineRecipe`
- `src/combine/data.ts` — populate recipe id from snapshot
- `src/graph/snapshot.ts` — ensure recipe ids are exposed
- `src/app/globals.css` — ReactionButtons styling + Tell-us-why chip
- Tests: `src/combine/__tests__/useRecipeReactions.test.ts` (optional; integration-style), extend existing bundle tests to verify `id` is populated

### Scale of the PR

This is a bigger PR than the last few. I can land it in two slices if preferred:
1. **Slice A**: schema + API + hook + DiscoveryToast wiring (the moment with highest engagement). Report button stays in DetailCard as-is for now.
2. **Slice B**: DetailCard per-row + CollectionBook per-recipe-chip wiring. Pure UI reuse of the primitive.

Slice A delivers 80% of the value with a single surface change; Slice B expands.

Going with single-PR unless you say otherwise.

## Scope expansion — items too

User asked for item-level reactions alongside recipe reactions. Updating the plan:

### Schema change

Instead of `recipe_reactions`, a single polymorphic **`reactions`** table:

```sql
CREATE TYPE reaction_target AS ENUM ('recipe', 'item');

CREATE TABLE reactions (
  target_kind  reaction_target NOT NULL,
  target_id    UUID NOT NULL,          -- recipe.id or item.id depending on kind
  user_id      TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES "user"(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  value        SMALLINT NOT NULL CHECK (value IN (-1, 1)),
  reason       TEXT,
  created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  PRIMARY KEY (target_kind, target_id, user_id)
);
CREATE INDEX reactions_target_idx ON reactions(target_kind, target_id);
```

Trade-offs:
- **No FK to the target** (can't FK conditionally on an enum). Cleanup via trigger on items/recipes delete, or a periodic job. Stale rows are harmless.
- **Polymorphic over two tables** because the hook, API, UI primitive, and admin triage are all identical regardless of target. Adding a third target later (sources? kinds?) is just a new enum value.
- Matches the `(kind, ref)` pattern we just proposed for T-0083 (`user_acknowledgements`). Repeated shape = strong signal.

### API

- `POST /api/combine/reactions` body `{targetKind, targetId, value: -1|0|1, reason?}`.
- `GET /api/combine/reactions?recipe=a,b,c&item=x,y` → `{recipe: {id: {mine, up, down}}, item: {id: {...}}}`.
- Batched GET so DetailCard can fetch its recipe rows + its item in one round-trip.

### Hook

`useReactions({recipeIds, itemIds})` returns:
- `{recipeReactions: Map<id, state>, itemReactions: Map<id, state>, vote(target, id, value, reason?)}`.

Single hook, two indexed maps internally.

### UI

`<ReactionButtons target={{kind: 'recipe' | 'item', id}} value onVote onReport />` — same primitive, carries target in props.

### Surfaces (revised)

- **DiscoveryToast**: recipe reactions.
- **DetailCard**:

Root cause: `next build` prerenders `/_not-found` (src/app/not-found.tsx), which imports the DB client via `@/graph/live` → `./load`. The DB client throws at module load when `DATABASE_URL` is unset. title: Combine Move helper: add tap-to-select + preview (parity with tray)
body:
The Move helper currently only supports drag. Tap-select-then-tap-target (with preview glow on valid destinations) should work too, matching how the tray/hold slots behave.

Tray behavior to mirror:
- Tap a slot → sets `selectedSlot`; `computePreview` lights every empty cell where it would combine and every occupied cell where drop-on-top would combine (ghost output + `+N` badge).
- Tap a target cell → dispatches `place` or `drop-on`.
- Tap the same slot again → deselects.

Target Move-helper behavior:
- With Move active, tap a full board tile → select it as the move source (sets `moveMode.from`, lights previews on valid destinations including empty cells where the moved tile would combine and occupied cells where `matchOn` succeeds).
- Tap a target cell → dispatch `{type:"move", from, to}`.
- Tap the source again → deselect.
- Bare tap on empty with no source selected → still exits the helper (current behavior).
- Drag path stays intact.

Engine: no changes required — `move` already handles both move-to-empty and move-to-combine-on-top (`src/combine/engine.ts:978-1030`).

Files likely touched:
- `src/components/combine/CombineBoard.tsx` — `onCellTap` (`:960-1043`), `onCellPointerDown` (`:1345-1377`), new state or extension of `selectedSlot` to carry a board source.
- `src/components/combine/board-parts/types.ts` — `computePreview` needs to accept a board source and simulate the `from` cell as vacated (otherwise it misses unlocked adjacencies and falsely scores the source cell).
- `src/components/combine/board-parts/board/Board.tsx` — pass preview + a "moving" style for the selected source cell (`aria-pressed`, selected label).
- `src/components/combine/board-parts/board/TipLine.tsx` — copy already handles both pre/post-select states (`:29-33`); verify wording.

Gotchas:
- Preview must simulate `from` vacated, or it will under-match.
- `moveMode.from` is already used mid-drag; if tap-select reuses it, ensure an aborted drag resets it to `null` without tearing down the mode.
- `onCellPointerDown` currently fires the drag unconditionally in `moveMode`. For tap-vs-drag disambiguation, reuse the tray pattern (`dragRef.moved` + `suppressClick`).
- Accessibility: source cell needs `aria-pressed` and "selected" in `aria-label`, like `Tray.tsx:49-50`.

comments.body:
Approach:

1. Extend `computePreview` to accept an optional `boardSource: { cell: number } | null`. When present, simulate `from` cell vacated (null-out a cloned board before `matchAt`/`matchOn`) so the preview reflects what a move would do. When the source is on the board, the source cell itself is skipped in the preview loop.

2. In `CombineBoard.tsx`:
   - Add tap-vs-drag disambiguation to `onCellPointerDown`: in Move mode, if `moveMode.from == null` and the tile is full, arm a tentative drag (same ref dance as tray/hold), but don't yet set `moveMode.from`. If the pointer moves past threshold, promote to drag and set `moveMode.from` for the DragGhost affordance; if it ends without moving, fall through to the trailing click = tap-select.
   - `onCellTap` in Move mode:
     - If `moveMode.from == null` and the cell is full → set `moveMode.from = cell` (this becomes the tap-selection).
     - If `moveMode.from == cell` → deselect (back to `moveMode.from = null`), stay in mode.
     - If `moveMode.from != null` and target cell is a legal destination (empty with/without combine, or occupied with matchOn) → dispatch `{type:"move", from, to}`, then exit mode on success.
     - Bare tap on empty with `from == null` → still exits mode (preserve current behavior).

3. In `Board.tsx`:
   - When `moveMode.from != null`, pass the `preview` map through (already wired, just now populated for board source).
   - Source cell (`moving`) gets `aria-pressed=true` and " selected" appended to `aria-label`, like `Tray.tsx:49`.
   - `isMovable` on other full cells stays as-is when `from == null`; after selection, we want `.can`/`.over` glow on destinations (already handled by the preview pathway) and keep `.movable` cleared since "other full tiles" aren't move sources anymore in this step.

4. Drag path untouched beyond the pointerdown gating. The `suppressClick` + `dragRef.moved` pattern from tray carries over.

5. `TipLine` already handles both pre/post-select copy — no change.

6. End-of-mode: after a successful tap-driven move, clear `moveMode`. On a "nope" (tapping a cell the engine rejects), stay in mode with `from` still set so the user can pick another target.

No engine changes. No new state field; reusing `moveMode.from` for both drag and tap sources is fine because the drag path also set it mid-gesture — the one gotcha is making sure an aborted drag resets `from` to null (already does via the Escape path + mode toggle).

Landed.

Changes:
- `src/components/combine/board-parts/types.ts:33` — `computePreview` now accepts a `{ source: "board", cell }` variant. When present, it clones the board with the source cell nulled, skips that cell in the preview loop, and runs the same `matchAt` / `matchOn` scan. This both unlocks adjacencies the vacated source enables and prevents the source from falsely appearing as a destination.
- `src/components/combine/CombineBoard.tsx:1523` — `preview` useMemo gains a branch that, when Move is active, a tap-source is picked, and no drag is in flight, feeds the board source into `computePreview`.
- `src/components/combine/CombineBoard.tsx:999` — `onCellTap` Move branch rewritten: full cell + no source → select; same cell → deselect; different cell → dispatch `{type:"move", from, to}` if legal (and exit mode) or no-op if illegal (keep source selected). Empty cell + no source still exits the mode. `bundle` + `state.n` added to deps.
- `src/components/combine/CombineBoard.tsx:1355` — `onCellPointerDown` no longer sets `moveMode.from = cell` on pointerdown; it just arms the drag ref. It also now early-returns if `moveMode.from != null` so tap-targets after tap-select don't accidentally arm a second drag. Early-return also means tap flows for targets go through `onCellTap` directly.
- `src/components/combine/CombineBoard.tsx:1258` — pointermove threshold now promotes a board drag by calling `setMoveMode({ from: d.slot })` once the gesture crosses 7px, keeping the dashed/lift source styling in sync with the drag ghost.
- `src/components/combine/CombineBoard.tsx:1114` — Escape in Move mode first deselects the source (if any), then on a second press exits the mode. Mirrors the tray's selectedSlot → mode-close progression.
- `src/components/combine/board-parts/board/Board.tsx:185` — `moving` cell now reports `aria-pressed=true` and " selected to move" in `aria-label`.
- `src/components/combine/board-parts/board/TipLine.tsx:30` — copy changed from "Drag…" to "Tap or drag…" and from "Drop the X…" to "Tap a square to place the X…".

Tests: `npm run typecheck` clean; `npm test` 296/296 green (including the 86-test engine suite and dealer bot simulation).

Not verified in-browser: dev server is running on :3000 but I can't drive a browser from here. Recommend a quick smoke: start Move helper → tap a full cell (should lift + outline, destinations glow) → tap a glowing cell (moves) → start again, tap source twice (deselects), tap empty cell (exits). Drag path should still work unchanged.

Follow-ups not filed (small UX nit): if a drag releases on an invalid target, today it snaps back and exits Move mode. With tap-select users can retry — you might want parity (snap back, stay in mode). Leaving as-is since it's the existing behavior and the task didn't call for a change.

title: Combine: per-move timestamp stream for admin pacing analytics
body:
Record each Combine move's timestamp so admins can analyse pacing — not just totals. Payload shape on finished-run POST (augmenting the existing `/api/combine/result` body):

```
{
  startedAt: epoch-ms,           // when the run began (first deal)
  endedAt: epoch-ms,             // when `state.over` flipped
  moves: [
    { tMs: number, kind: "place"|"drop-on"|"move"|"clear"|"shore"|"pluck"|"hold"|"wipe"|"swap"|"undo"|"choose", ok?: boolean }
    // tMs = ms since startedAt. `ok` for the few actions the engine can nope.
  ]
}
```

Enables:
- Session duration (= `endedAt - startedAt`, or `last tMs - first tMs`).
- Time-per-move distributions; stall detection; drag-vs-tap latency once we tag input mode.
- Feeds T-0035 Combine dashboards (median session, per-age pacing, timeout-loss for Fast).

**Load-bearing concerns (overlap with T-0012 / T-0027):**
- **Trust boundary is the same as the score.** `/api/combine/result` already trusts client-posted totals with only clamps (see `src/app/api/combine/result/route.ts:13-17`). This stream is strictly more detailed telemetry — a hostile client can fabricate it as easily as it can fabricate the score. So:
  - **Admin-only until replay/HMAC ships.** Store it, surface it in admin, but don't make any public (leaderboard / profile) signal depend on it.
  - **Don't let timing gate eligibility** (e.g., "ran too fast → disqualify") until the whole run is server-verified — adversaries would just slow their forgeries down. Noted in T-0012.
  - **When T-0012's replay/HMAC lands**, the timestamp stream is exactly what a server-side replay would consume to validate pacing plausibility. Design the schema now so it slots in later.
- **Payload size.** Typical run is 50–300 moves; at ~16 bytes/entry serialised, that's ~1–5 KB per run. Fine. Cap at 2000 entries server-side to defend against crafted megabodies.
- **Privacy.** No PII — move kinds and ms deltas only. No cursor coords or dwell heatmaps. Keep it that way to avoid child-profile-adjacent data per CLAUDE.md.

**Storage:**
- Easiest: new nullable JSONB column on `progress`, e.g. `trace` — keeps the single-row-per-run shape and T-0012's queries unchanged. Or a sibling `progress_traces` table keyed by progress id if we want to lazy-load (heavy trace columns can slow leaderboard aggregates).
- Lean toward sibling table so leaderboard reads never pay the trace cost.

**Client side:**
- `CombineBoard.tsx` tracks a `movesRef.current: Array<{tMs:number, kind:string, ok?:boolean}>` and `startedAtRef.current: number`. Push on every `act(...)` that reaches the engine (not on no-ops like suppressed clicks). Reset at run start / restart.
- Debug + fast mode currently bypass `/api/combine/result`; keep bypass consistent (Fast is score-only by design; see memory `project_combine_fast_mode.md`). Decision needed: do we want traces for Fast? Lean yes — it's the mode most likely to attract anomalies.
- Resumed-from-localStorage runs lose their trace history. Options: (a) persist the trace alongside the save blob, (b) accept that resumed runs upload partial traces with `startedAt=null` so admin tools can flag them. Lean (a) — bytes are cheap.

**Admin surface (ties into T-0035):**
- Per-run detail page: timeline strip of moves with icon per kind, vertical line per age-up, a density plot of inter-move latency.
- Aggregate rollups: p50/p90 run duration per theme per age; moves-per-minute distribution; stall-cluster detection.

**Open:**
- Visibility-change handling: do we pause the clock when the tab is hidden (T-0032 pauses audio)? If we don't, a backgrounded tab inflates duration enormously. Lean yes — pause clock + log a `blur`/`focus` event pair in the stream so the gap is explicit.
- Clock source: `performance.now()` for monotonic deltas (`tMs` = `now - start`), then one `Date.now()` for `startedAt`/`endedAt` wall-clock anchors.

**Depends on / related:**
- T-0035 (admin analytics home — this is a data source)
- T-0012 (public leaderboard — must stay admin-only until this gate ships)
- T-0027 (persistence audit — same trust boundary)
- T-0032 (visibility pause — influences clock handling)

title: Combine: "ship off board" affordance for 1-input recipes (e.g. star → supernova → sulfur)
body:
Some items are unreachable because their only producing recipe has a single ingredient — nothing on the board combines *with* them, and drop-on-top needs two tiles. The star → supernova → sulfur chain is the canonical case. Today the player can only wait for the dealer to hand the item, which doesn't help if the item is itself an output that needs promoting.

**The affordance:**
- When a board tile is the sole ingredient of a known 1-input recipe, let the player trigger the transform directly.
- UX: reuse the recipe-ambiguity picker (same visual grammar as the existing ChoicePicker), but with one option + an explicit "send off / promote" button. When multiple 1-input recipes exist for the same tile, show them all as choices like today.
- Trigger surface: tap the tile with nothing selected (currently opens info card) → add a "Make → <output>" row in the DetailCard. Keep info-card access via long-press on the tile. (Alternative: dedicated board-tile menu — needs design pass.)

**Cost / turn semantics (pick one before implementation):**
- Free + counts as a turn, like `place` / `drop-on`: preserves game pressure, treats promotion as a regular move.
- Free + no turn, like `move` helper: the player has no alternative path, so arguably it's more "the game owed me this" than a real choice. Risks: trivial to spam if free + no turn when a tile happens to be on the board.
- Recommendation: counts as a turn. The chain star → supernova → sulfur still takes 2 turns to resolve, mirroring 2 placements.

**Which link types qualify as "1-input"?** Likely all five (`f`, `w`, `n`, `s`, `e`) when the recipe's `all.length === 1`. Needs a quick audit of the current graph to see how many 1-input recipes exist and whether any should be excluded (e.g., should `w`-only "used-with" promotions count, or only `f` / `e`?).

**Where it lives in the engine:**
- New action `{type: "promote", cell}` in `src/combine/engine.ts`. Reuses `resolveMatch` with a synthesised match of one cell. The `choosing` path already handles multi-output recipes — if the single ingredient has multiple 1-input recipes, go through `choosing` the same way as drop-on.
- Discovery / seal logic unchanged (`sealIfDiscovered` runs after).
- Score: same formula as a regular combine so leaderboards stay comparable.

**Preview / UI:**
- In computePreview, a selected tile that has a known 1-input recipe could glow in-place. A "ship" badge on the cell signals "promote here." Or skip preview and rely on the DetailCard button — simpler v1.
- Pictogram / `+N` badge on the tile for alternatives, same grammar as the ambiguity picker.

**Accessibility:**
- aria-label the promote button clearly: "Promote <item> into <output>."
- Keyboard: Enter on a focused promotable tile opens the DetailCard with the Promote button focused.

**Dealer implications:**
- The dealer currently assumes all recipes have ≥2 ingredients when picking partners (`src/combine/deal.ts:118-129`, `:155-180`). 1-input recipes don't participate in the partner-pool logic — they're produced by the player via the new action, not by dealer-fed tray tiles. Check: do 1-input recipes exist in `A.recipes` today? If so, they're effectively dead for pathing and only reachable via the new affordance.

**Testing:**
- Golden path: place star, promote to supernova, promote to sulfur, all three in collection.
- Multi-recipe 1-input: pick a tile whose single ingredient has two known outputs → ChoicePicker opens → each promotes correctly.
- Unknown 1-input recipe: player hasn't seen the output yet → still show a "Make something?" option (or hide, per spec decision), matching the preview rule for 2-input recipes where unknown outputs don't glow.

**Open questions:**
- Should the promote button appear if the player hasn't discovered the output yet? Mirrors the preview policy for 2-input recipes.
- Cost: counts as a turn, or free? (Recommendation above: counts as a turn.)
- How is the action surfaced in the TopBar / helpers menu, if at all? Probably not — it's a property of the tile, not a helper.
- Does it apply to tiles in the tray / hold too, or board-only? Lean board-only for v1 — tray / hold placement already implicitly chooses where to promote.

**Related:**
- T-0001 (recipe-complexity options at run start) — "drop 1-input recipes" could become one of those toggles.
- T-0034 (discovery notifications) — same surface for the "new collection" moment after a promote.
- T-0066 (Move helper tap-select) — same ChoicePicker pattern on a board-sourced action.

comments.body:
Audit findings + approach:

**Current state:** `src/combine/data.ts:73` filters `all.length < 2 || all.length > 7` — 1-input recipes are **stripped from bundles entirely**, which is why star → supernova is unreachable. The data layer has them (confirmed: `items.data.ts` has `supernova` with `f:["star"]`, `neutron star merger` with `f:["supernova"]`, and the full heavy-element chain below).

**Design decisions made (reversible):**
1. **Action semantics:** Promote costs a turn (consumes 1 move), scores via the existing `finishResolve` formula. For `recipe.all.length === 1`, the formula `20 * tier * mult * (1 + 0.5*(len-2))` yields `0.5` × base — so a promote scores half of a pair combine. Matches "worth less than a two-tile combine" intuition.
2. **Auto-fire guard:** `matchAt` with a 1-input recipe would fire the moment the ingredient lands on an empty cell (because `need = []` → `grow` returns the seed cell with zero work). That would turn every `star` placement into an auto-supernova — hidden chain, loses the "ship it off" moment. Fix: **exclude 1-input recipes from `matchAt` and `matchOn`** so they only fire through the new `promote` action.
3. **Visibility rule:** promote option appears only if the output is in `found ∪ collection` (mirrors preview-glow policy for 2-input recipes). Unknown 1-input recipes stay hidden until something else shows the player the output.
4. **Where it surfaces:** DetailCard for a board-sourced tile gains a "Promote → <output>" primary button (or a list if multiple). Opened by tap on board tile with nothing selected — the existing info-card flow. Long-press / Escape semantics unchanged.
5. **Scope:** v1 is board-only. Tray/hold tiles promote implicitly via `place` (and `matchAt` gate we add will keep auto-fire off — the player still has to then open DetailCard and tap Promote).

**Plan:**
1. `src/combine/data.ts:73` — accept `all.length === 1`.
2. `src/combine/match.ts:70, 92` — skip recipes with `r.all.length < 2` in both `matchAt` and `matchOn`. Doc the reason.
3. `src/combine/engine.ts` — new `{type:"promote", cell}` action. Looks up `byIngredient[tile]`, filters for `r.all.length === 1`, dispatches via `resolveMatch` (which already handles multi-alternative → `choosing`). Costs a move, runs `afterMove`, seals discoveries.
4. `src/combine/engine.ts` — `alternatives()` for 1-input recipes: it already groups by `[...r.all].sort().join("+")` which is just `[ingredient]` — so sibling 1-input outputs stack. Good.
5. `src/components/combine/board-parts/overlays/DetailCard.tsx` — "Promote to X" button when `bundle.byIngredient[id]` contains any 1-input recipe whose output is known. Dispatches `{type:"promote", cell}`.
6. `src/components/combine/CombineBoard.tsx` — pass `onPromote(cell)` to DetailCard when the current `infoTile` originated from a board tap (need to track that — currently `infoTile` is just the id). Add a `boardInfoCell: number | null` sibling state.
7. Tests:
   - `data.test.ts` — bundle includes 1-input recipes (e.g., supernova).
   - `engine.test.ts` — promote action: happy path, unknown output guard, multi-recipe choosing path, cost-a-turn, score formula.
   - `match.test.ts` — matchAt/matchOn now skip 1-input recipes.
   - `deal.test.ts` — dealer still produces playable trays with 1-input recipes present (should be unaffected since partner loops naturally yield 0).

**Dealer side effect:** 1-input recipes have `r.all = [x]`. Dealer partner loops iterate `r.all` excluding the pile tile — zero iterations, zero partners added. So 1-input recipes contribute nothing to dealer partner pools. `playsInOne`/`playsInTwo` currently test `matchAt`/`matchOn` which we'll gate to `>= 2` ingredients — so the dealer's play-guarantee logic won't falsely consider a 1-input recipe a "play." Safe.

**Open questions settled while auditing — ping if you disagree:**
- Promote costs a turn (not free).
- Auto-fire is disabled via `matchAt`/`matchOn` gate — explicit action only.
- v1 is board-only; no tray/hold affordance.
- Hidden until output is in `found ∪ collection`.

Landed (behind one open design call — see bottom).

**Files changed:**
- `src/combine/data.ts:73` — accept `all.length === 1`. 1-input recipes now flow into bundles (115 recipes / 112 new outputs in Everything; `outputs.size` 203 → 377).
- `src/combine/match.ts:70, 92` — `matchAt` and `matchOn` skip recipes with `r.all.length < 2`. Placing a `star` on the board no longer auto-transforms to `supernova`; promote is the only path.
- `src/combine/engine.ts` — new `{type:"promote", cell, known?}` action. Filters 1-input recipes for `tile`; narrows to outputs the player knows (`state.found` ∪ caller-supplied `known`); fires immediately if one is known, opens a `choosing` picker if multiple. Costs a move, scores via existing `finishResolve` (which yields 0.5× pair-match points for 1-input — authored by the formula, not a special-case).
- `src/components/combine/board-parts/overlays/DetailCard.tsx` — new optional `onPromote` prop. Renders a "Make X" button when the tile has at least one known 1-input output and the card was opened for a board cell. Aria-label includes both input and output names.
- `src/components/combine/CombineBoard.tsx` — new `infoCell: number | null` sibling state so the DetailCard knows whether it was opened by a board tap. Only board-sourced info cards receive `onPromote`. All existing `setInfoTile(null)` sites now also clear `infoCell`.
- `src/combine/__tests__/engine.test.ts` — 7 new promote tests (immediate fire, unknown guard, lifetime override, choosing path, empty cell, known filter, matchAt guard on placement).
- `src/combine/__tests__/data.test.ts` — bounds widened for `outputs.size`; new regression guard asserting star → supernova exists as a 1-input recipe; renamed "every recipe has 2..7 ingredients" → "1..7".

**Tests:** `npm run typecheck` clean; `npm test` 304/304 (up from 296 — 7 promote + 1 data regression).

**UX (direct answer to your question):**
1. Place a star on the board (dealer still hands them out as before — 1-input recipes don't participate in partner pools so the dealer is unchanged).
2. Tap the star → DetailCard opens → "Make supernova" button appears **if you've already discovered supernova**. Tap it → star becomes supernova. Costs one turn.
3. Tap the supernova → "Make sulfur / iron / silicon / oxygen / …" — the ChoicePicker opens with every known 1-input output. Pick one.
4. Rinse, repeat. Costs one turn per promote.

**Open design call — needs your decision:**
Current gating: Promote button only appears for outputs the player has already discovered. That's symmetric with 2-input preview glow, but it creates a chicken-and-egg: **a brand-new player can never discover supernova via promote** because the button requires knowing supernova. The only way in is via Explore (web) or future daily puzzle seeding.

Two choices:
- **(A) Always show "Make something?" for unknown 1-input outputs.** Promote fires and reveals the new item. Spoiler risk is tiny — the player learns *that* a promotion exists for this tile, not what it makes. Recommendation.
- **(B) Keep current gating.** Players must learn 1-input chains externally first. Cleaner principle, worse discoverability.

I did not implement (A) yet — it's a 10-line change in both engine (drop the `known` filter when the caller sets a flag) and DetailCard (render the button with a generic label) but it inverts the surface area so wanted your sign-off first.

**Secondary follow-up candidates (not filed):**
- Visual affordance on the board tile itself (e.g., subtle "⬆" badge) when it has a known promote, so the player doesn't have to tap every tile to discover affordances.
- Lifetime collection reachability: the `known` param of `promote` already flows through, so tap in UI already passes `knownIds` which includes lifetime collection. That's wired.
- Audit: double-check `supernova` isn't tagged `combine-exclude` in some theme spec — otherwise the regression test would false-fail later. Not seen in `items.data.ts`.

Final landing comment (post-review iterations).

**Design evolution during review:**
1. **Entry point:** initial plan put "Promote" as a button inside DetailCard. Reversed on your feedback — DetailCard is info, not action. Switched to **tap = promote, long-press = info** on board tiles, mirroring the tray's grammar.
2. **Discovery gating:** initial implementation only offered known outputs (chicken-and-egg: never could first-discover supernova in-game). Flipped to option (A): all 1-input recipes are eligible on promote; the ChoicePicker ranks known first and hides unknown names behind a "Something new" placeholder.
3. **Cancellable choosing:** picker had no backout. Added `ChoosingState.cancellable: true` on promote; new `{type:"cancel-choice"}` action rolls back via `lastSnapshot`. Place/drop-on/move pickers stay modal (already-consumed tiles can't cleanly rewind).
4. **Self-ref collapse:** "water → paper" surfaced because `recycled paper` is `paper + water → paper`; dropping self-ref left a bogus 1-input. `recipeParts` now returns `hadSelfRef` and the caller refuses collapsed 1-input survivors.
5. **howMade stale:** first-make-only semantics meant the DetailCard highlighted the wrong recipe variant after a promote on a tile first made via a 2-input recipe (or resumed from save). Changed `howMade` to **update on every make**, so it reads as "last made from" (which the UI now shows).
6. **DetailCard shows all variants:** previously one recipe (first match by bundle order). Now renders every known variant as a chip row, with the player's last-used path outlined in accent blue + tinted background.
7. **Visibility badge:** a tap-to-promote tile is invisible without affordance. Added `.pmk` corner badge (opposite corner from crumble `.crk`) with an up-arrow SVG and a count badge for ≥2 recipes. Hidden during fx (fuse/crumble/pop/ship/moving) so transient animations stay legible.

**Final file list:**
- `src/combine/data.ts` — filter accepts `all.length === 1`; `recipeParts` exposes `hadSelfRef`; self-ref collapse rejected. `_recipeParts_FOR_TEST` export.
- `src/combine/match.ts` — `matchAt`/`matchOn` skip 1-input recipes (no auto-fire on placement).
- `src/combine/engine.ts` — new `{type:"promote", cell}` and `{type:"cancel-choice"}` actions; `ChoosingState.cancellable`; `howMade` updates on every make.
- `src/components/combine/board-parts/board/Board.tsx` — `.pmk` badge render + `aria-label` announcement.
- `src/components/combine/board-parts/overlays/DetailCard.tsx` — rewritten to render all known recipe variants, highlighting the last-used one.
- `src/components/combine/board-parts/overlays/ChoicePicker.tsx` — optional `onCancel` button when `state.choosing.cancellable`.
- `src/components/combine/CombineBoard.tsx` — tap/long-press board handling, cancel-choice wiring (click + Escape), `infoCell` sibling state.
- `src/app/globals.css` — `.pmk` badge styles, `.cbchip.used` highlight.

**Test coverage (12 new tests + 1 reshaped suite, 315 total up from 296):**
- Engine (`engine.test.ts`): promote unknown-reveal, immediate-fire single, choosing path (multiple), empty cell no-op, no-1-input no-op, over-run no-op, fast-mode no-collection, scoring formula (0.5× pair = 21 pts for tier M), matchAt placement guard, cancel-choice rollback, cancel-choice no-op on non-cancellable, howMade overwrites on repeat make.
- Data (`data.test.ts`): star → supernova regression, water → paper self-ref guard, no bundle 1-input came from a self-ref collapse (cross-cutting), `recipeParts` self-ref flag set, `recipeParts` clean 1-input unflagged, water promotes only legit paths (hydrogen-gas electrolysis, ultrapure water).
- Dealer (`deal.test.ts`): water-piled board still produces ≥98% playable trays (1-input recipes don't poison partner selection).

**Known gaps (not filed as follow-ups — flag if you'd like me to):**
- No RTL/E2E tests for the UI paths (tap-to-promote, long-press-for-info, Escape cancel) — consistent with the rest of the codebase; CombineBoard has no component tests today.
- Engine doesn't gate dispatch on `state.choosing` at the top of the reducer; UI relies on the ChoicePicker overlay being visually blocking. Latent not-a-bug today, but a tighter guard would belt-and-brace.

**Tests:** `npm run typecheck` clean; `npm test` 315/315.

title: Add React error boundaries across the app
body:
Wrap key routes/surfaces in error boundaries so a render-time crash shows a graceful fallback instead of blanking the page.

Scope to consider:
- Top-level app boundary (App Router `error.tsx` files per route segment)
- Combine board (`src/components/combine/board-parts/board/Board.tsx` and friends) — crashes here kill an active run
- Admin surfaces (`/admin/tree`, `/admin/kinds`, `/admin/combine/themes`, `/admin/items/[id]`)
- Explore / item pages (`/i/[slug]`, `/explore/[slug]`)
- Craft and Daily link pages

Each boundary should:
- Log to PostHog via the typed `track()` helper (no PII)
- Offer a retry / reload action
- Degrade gracefully (don't lose unrelated UI when one region errors)

Open questions:
- Shared `<AppErrorBoundary>` component vs. per-route `error.tsx` files (likely both: global fallback + targeted client boundaries for interactive subtrees like Combine board)
- How to surface errors in dev vs. prod
