title: Live snapshot: invalidate on out-of-band DB writes (LISTEN/NOTIFY)
body:
`src/graph/live.ts` caches the live Snapshot in-process forever once built (`slot.current` returned on every call to `getLiveSnapshot()`). `reloadSnapshot()` exists but is only called from admin mutation routes — so any write that bypasses those routes (one-shot migration scripts, direct SQL, future cron jobs) leaves the running Node process serving a stale graph until the service restarts.

Concrete symptom (T-0157 follow-up): after running `migrate-plant-origins.js` against prod, admin tree showed the new pig→mammals edge (reads DB directly) but `/i/pig` still showed empty "up" column, 0 ancestors, and a 6-hop path routed only through pre-existing down edges. Resolved only by a service restart.

The right fix is the one already flagged in the file header (src/graph/live.ts:7-8): a Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY channel that fires on content writes and triggers `reloadSnapshot()` on every replica.

Scope:
1. Pick a channel name (e.g. `kb_changed`).
2. On the writer side: emit `NOTIFY kb_changed` from admin mutation routes AND from the one-shot migration helper (so scripts don't need bespoke handling). Simplest wiring is a small helper that any write path can call after commit.
3. On the reader side: a long-lived `postgres.listen()` subscriber started at module load in `live.ts`, which calls `reloadSnapshot()` (debounced — many writes in one admin session shouldn't kick off N rebuilds). Needs to survive connection drops (auto-reconnect + rebuild on reconnect to catch missed events).
4. Expose a tiny admin endpoint `POST /api/admin/snapshot/reload` as a manual fallback for "I ran raw SQL, force-refresh now" cases.
5. Keep the current `reloadSnapshot()` export for tests + fallback.

Open questions to resolve in the approach comment:
- Debounce window (200ms? 1s?).
- What happens mid-rebuild if NOTIFY fires again — queue a second rebuild or drop?
- Do we also want to piggyback on this to invalidate other derived caches (closed set, kind pictograms, code maps) — all of which are rebuilt by `buildLive()` today, so the answer is probably "already handled, because reloadSnapshot calls buildLive".

Relates to T-0157 (plant-origins ship). Preconditions for safely rolling out more out-of-band migration scripts and for multi-replica deploys (CLAUDE.md hard rule: "If you add replicas, move the counters to Postgres and reload snapshots through LISTEN/NOTIFY").

title: Combine "flat" mode prototype: full-pool dealer + unique-count progression
body:
Prototype of the T-0135 proposal: remove band gating from the dealer so it samples from the full theme item pool; replace band-based age progression with unique-find count thresholds.

Sim data (see T-0135 comments) showed board-aware full-pool sampling gives:
- 10x tile variety per run (259 unique tiles vs 25 baseline).
- ~2x discovery rate per 400 moves (102 vs 47).
- Combo rate drops 70% → 48% (acceptable).

### Scope

Behind a feature flag so the user can toggle in dev and compare feel. The flag defaults off; current banded mode is unchanged for all production players.

**Code touches:**
- `src/combine/data.ts` — `ageSets(bundle, age)` returns full-pool sets when flag is on (instead of `dealBands = {age, age+1}` filtered sets).
- `src/combine/engine.ts` — age-up condition: when flag on, age-up on `state.found.length >= thresholds[state.age + 1]`. Thresholds default to `[0, 10, 25, 50, 100, 175, 275, 400]` (each age adds +50% more discoveries than the last).
- Flag plumbing: a `flat` bool on `GameState` (or a module-level `isFlatMode()` reading from env/localStorage/URL param). Prefer URL param + localStorage for easy dev toggling without rebuild.
- `src/combine/types.ts` — add a `Mode` extension or a separate `progression: "banded" | "flat"` field.

**Explicitly out of scope:**
- No changes to daily mode (still uses target-list; flat mode is endless-only for the prototype).
- No content migration (bands remain for catalogue grouping).
- No changes to helpers/scoring/crumble logic.

### Acceptance

- Flag toggles between banded and flat modes without restart (dev convenience).
- Flat mode: user plays a Combine game, sees a mixed board drawn from the whole theme, age-up fires on unique-find thresholds.
- Both modes pass existing tests.
- A short note in the task comment on how to toggle.

Follow-up decisions deferred: formal rollout plan, helper scaling tweaks, daily rework, progression-UI changes.

comments.body:
## Landed — flat mode behind a flag

### How to toggle in dev

Append `?flat=1` to any Combine URL (e.g. `http://localhost:3000/combine?flat=1`). The flag persists to localStorage — subsequent navigations stay in flat mode without the query param. Flip back with `?flat=0`, or clear `combine_flat` from localStorage.

Headless/sim path: `CB_FLAT=1 npx tsx ...`.

### Files

- **`src/combine/flat.ts`** (new, ~60 lines): `isFlatMode()` reads URL param → localStorage → `process.env.CB_FLAT`. `FLAT_THRESHOLDS = [0, 10, 25, 50, 90, 150, 225, 325, 450]` controls age-up pacing. `flatNeed(age)` returns the cumulative unique-find count to leave age `age`.

- **`src/combine/data.ts`** (`ageSets`): in flat mode returns the full theme pool — all recipes, all ingredients — ignoring band. Dealer, crumble, hint all see the full set. Shape of the return is unchanged so the rest of the engine runs as-is.

- **`src/combine/engine.ts`** (`afterMove`): age-up condition switches to `state.found.length >= flatNeed(state.age)` when the flag is on. Final-age victory branch is skipped in flat mode (progression is open-ended).

### Sim validation (`CB_FLAT=1 promote-sim`)

| metric | baseline | flat mode |
|---|---|---|
| age 0 most-repeated tile count | 21 | **5** |
| age 0 trays to leave | 44 | **20** |
| age 1 most-repeated | 33 | **11** |
| age-2 reach | 73% of runs | **80%** |
| unique tiles per run | 25 (6% of pool) | **45–373+** (depending on dealer mode) |

The engine-level sim shows the same shape as the earlier board-aware random sim: diversity up, repetition way down, progression faster but still graded. Trace shows mixed-era tiles: `[lithium, helium, oxygen]`, `[package substrate, packaging plant, calcium]` — exactly the "mixed board" the user hypothesized.

### Design consequences (worth knowing while playtesting)

1. **No crumble in flat mode.** `A.USE` in flat is the entire theme pool, so every tile is always "in use" and never crumbles. If this makes the board feel too forgiving, we can either keep crumble timing on all tiles unconditionally or add a flat-mode-specific rule (e.g. crumble after N moves regardless of age).
2. **Final-age ending disabled.** In banded mode, finishing the last age ends the run with a flourish. Flat mode doesn't end on age, so a run ends only on stuck/board-full. Fine for prototype playtesting; may want a soft cap later.
3. **Catalogue still groups by band** — collection view is unchanged. Players will see items in thematic bands even if they discovered them out of order.
4. **Daily mode unchanged.** Daily already uses target-list ending (`state.target`). `isFlatMode()` is independent of mode, so you can combine `?flat=1` with daily — but the sampler change is the main thing; daily's own progression is target-based.
5. **Helpers scale by `bandSize(age)`** which uses `outBand` from the KB. In flat mode this is still well-defined (unchanged); helpers grant on each age-up based on how populous the "arriving" band is.
6. **The dealer's board-aware Layer 2** now has the full pool to partner with. This is what makes flat mode feel good: mixed board + full pool = always a partner.

### Not touched

- No new tests (prototype only; existing 386 tests all pass with flag off).
- No UI changes: no visible "flat mode" indicator, no settings toggle. If you decide to productize this, we'd want a user-visible switch.
- No reseed / content migration.

### Checks

- `npm run typecheck`: clean.
- `npm test`: 386/386 pass (flag reads `CB_FLAT` env; tests set nothing, so they run as banded, unchanged).
- `CB_FLAT=1 promote-sim`: end-to-end run through the real engine completes, ages up on unique counts, produces mixed-band trays.

### What to look for while playtesting

- **Does the mixed board feel exciting or chaotic?** Core UX question.
- **Does the combo rate (~48% in sim vs 70% baseline) feel sluggish or just varied?**
- **Does age-up at N discoveries feel earned, or arbitrary?** Threshold list is a first guess; tune in `flat.ts`.
- **Any confusion when a late-era item appears early?** E.g. seeing "copper wire" in age 0.

## Playtest outcome + reverting

User played flat mode in dev. Verdict: "sampling is better (more diverse) but the logical progression of learning things isn't there, we have so many different things." Flat mode trades thematic ladder for breadth — the breadth works, the lost "building up" feeling is a real cost.

### Why we're closing + reverting

The design question "is flat the right progression model?" got answered: no, not as implemented. But we also realised the sim can't reliably answer design questions like this because it models a greedy player with no hold, helpers, undo, or planning. Before we commit to any progression redesign (flat / soft-band / banded-with-content-migration), we need better sim fidelity.

Continuing in **T-0162 — Strategic Combine simulator** (hold / helpers / undo / lookahead). Once strategic data is in hand, we revisit progression design.

### What to revert

- `src/combine/data.ts` — `ageSets` flat-mode branch + `isFlatMode` import.
- `src/combine/engine.ts` — flat age-up branch + `flat`/`flatNeed` imports.
- Keep `src/combine/flat.ts` as a reference for the eventual `?gp_override=` system.

### Keeping

- `src/combine/__tests__/promote-sim.ts` — useful, will extend in T-0162.
- `src/combine/__tests__/random-sampler-sim.ts` — useful for histogram comparison.
- `src/combine/flat.ts` — unused but demonstrates the flag pattern.

Marking done + will revert engine/data changes as part of T-0162 kickoff.

title: Strategic Combine simulator: hold, helpers, undo, lookahead
body:
Current sims (`simulate.ts`, `promote-sim.ts`, `random-sampler-sim.ts`) model a greedy player: best immediate move, no planning, no hold, no helpers, no undo. This is insufficient fidelity for the design decisions we're currently making (flat vs banded vs soft-banded progression). A "good" greedy player and a real strategic player may experience the game very differently — repetition that feels crushing to a greedy sim may be fine for a strategic one, or vice versa.

Build a strategic headless player on top of the existing engine. Keep everything in TypeScript; no Python/RL yet (deferred until after we confirm heuristic sim is insufficient).

### Scope

Extend `src/combine/__tests__/promote-sim.ts` (or spin up a new `strategic-sim.ts`) with:

1. **Hold policy.** Hold a tile when:
   - It has an unfound output reachable via a 1-input promote (bank the discovery).
   - It's the only partner for a piled tile and the current tray doesn't let me place both.
   - The current tray has a better combine than placing this tile raw.
   Cap holds at `holdCapacity(age)`.

2. **Helper usage.** Use:
   - `swap` when tray has no combine and no placement improves board state.
   - `clear` / `pluck` when a single tile blocks multiple matches.
   - `wipe` (if unlocked) when board is dominated by one pile and no partner is incoming.
   - `hint` when stuck.
   - `shore` on a soon-to-crumble tile that's still needed.
   Model helper scarcity: these are earned on age-up, can run out.

3. **Undo policy.** Undo a move when the resulting state has fewer combinable moves than the pre-move state AND no discovery fired. (Models "oh wait, that was bad.")

4. **1-step lookahead for combine choice.** When multiple combines are available, prefer the one whose output has the best follow-up — pair with a tile already on-board, or starts a chain.

5. **Age-aware goals.** Instead of pure greedy, the player has a soft goal: "make N more unique things in the current age to level up." Weights toward moves that produce current-age outputs.

### Validation

Re-run the baseline / flat / existing-levers comparisons from T-0135 under the strategic player. Key questions:

- Does the "age 0 grind" (currently 55 moves in greedy-sim) reduce under strategic play?
- Does flat mode still look like a win when the player can hold + use helpers to smooth greedy play?
- Does any lever previously rejected (overlap-2, heavy-ban 0.5) actually help a strategic player even if it hurts a greedy one?

### Explicitly not in scope

- No RL / Python env. If this strategic player isn't enough to inform the decision, that's the follow-up.
- No new UI. Sim only.
- No `?gp_override` plumbing yet — that's a separate task once we know what overrides matter.

### Prerequisite / cleanup

Revert the T-0161 flat-mode plumbing first (ageSets branch + engine age-up branch). We want baseline sim data before layering changes back on. Keep `src/combine/flat.ts` as a reference pattern for the eventual `gp_override` system but unwire it from `data.ts` and `engine.ts`.

comments.body:
## Strategic sim landed + first results

Reverted T-0161 flat-mode plumbing. Built `src/combine/__tests__/strategic-sim.ts` with hold, helpers, undo, and lookahead. Headline numbers from 30 games, Everything endless:

| Metric | Greedy | Strategic | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| Discoveries per run | 42.2 | **47.8** | +14% |
| Final age | 1.47 | **1.80** | +22% |
| Moves per run | 154 | 222 | +44% |
| Runs completed (not stuck) | 0/30 | **12/30** | 40% completion rate |
| Hold uses | 0 | 21.2 | — |
| Swap uses | 0 | 5.0 | — |
| Clear uses | 0 | 2.8 | — |
| Undo uses | 0 | 1.0 | — |
| Unique tiles per run | 22 | 31 | +41% |
| **Most-repeated tile count** | 48.6 | **71.6** | **+47% worse** |
| **Trays dealt per run** | 134 | **193** | +44% more |

### What this tells us

1. **The strategic player progresses significantly further.** 40% of runs complete vs 0% greedy — the game ends on final-age victory instead of hard-stuck. This is a big fidelity gain over the greedy sim; prior sims simulated a player who gives up too easily.

2. **Hold is heavily used (21 uses/run)** — mostly to bank promote discoveries. This confirms real players would feel the hold mechanic as central to progression, not optional. The prior greedy sim was understating the game's playability.

3. **The repetition problem is WORSE under strategic play, not better.** Counterintuitive but makes sense: the strategic player survives longer, so they see more trays (193 vs 134), and the same ~5-tile dominant set shows up in more of them (oxygen in 71 trays, not 48). Grinding feel scales with survival time.

4. **Tile diversity is still terrible.** 31 of 397 items (~8%) are seen per run under strategic play. 365 items (92% of the pool) never appear once.

### What this means for the design question

The user's "bands 1-2 feel grindy" complaint is now *even more* validated for strategic players. Both greedy and strategic sim players see:
- The same ~5 dominant tiles (H, O, C, water, He) occupying most of their tray view.
- The same massive gap between content that exists (397 items) and content seen (22-31 items/run).

The sim fidelity gain **did not invalidate the earlier design finding** that bands 1-2 are structurally repetitive. It strengthened it: the strategic player is actually *more* exposed to the grind because they play longer runs.

### What the strategic sim *didn't* fix

Still missing:
- **Move selection heuristics are hand-coded.** A real player might pursue specific recipes ("I want to make 'glass' so I'll chase the ingredients"). Our player is still reactive.
- **Learning curve isn't modelled.** All runs use the same policy. First-game vs 50th-game player strategies would differ.
- **No "I'm bored" signal.** The main thing players complain about — the feel of repetition — we're still measuring proxies for (most-repeated-count, exact-repeats) not the actual UX.

### Suggested next step

Re-run the flat / content-migration / dealer-tweak comparisons under the strategic sim to see if any option looks different now:

1. **Flat mode** under strategic play — does the "lost progression" feeling show up quantitatively? Expect: discoveries go way up, final-age N/A (no bands), hold usage changes shape.
2. **Content migration (lever 4a)** — virtually move 24 reflexives to later bands, re-sim strategic play. Expect: bands 1-2 become faster, repetition shifts to new bottlenecks.
3. **Dealer diversity tweaks** (heavy-ban, overlap-reject) under strategic play — any that previously hurt greedy may help strategic.

Will proceed with #1 (fastest to measure) unless redirected.

title: Soft-bands Combine prototype: discovery-reachable pool
body:
Successor to T-0161 (flat mode). Instead of either hard bands or no bands, the dealer samples from a **reachability-defined pool** that grows as the player discovers:

- **Known set** = items the player has combined with OR discovered this run, plus the initial seed tiles (BASE).
- **Reachable set** = known ∪ one recipe hop out: any ingredient x where some recipe r has x ∈ r.all AND ≥1 other ingredient in r.all is already known. Also includes the outputs of recipes whose ingredients are entirely in known.
- **Dealer pool** = reachable set, biased toward recipes that use something in known.

Age-up uses unique-find thresholds (like flat), but scaled to KB size (e.g. age up every ceil(totalItems * fractionPerAge) finds), keeping age count stable as KB grows.

### Why this is the right shape

- **Progression is logical** (user constraint 3): you only see tiles one hop from what you know. Early on it's just BASE; after discovering water, water-using recipes' partners show up.
- **Scales with KB** (user constraint 2): the growing-pool rule is graph-local, not band-dependent. Bigger KBs just mean the pool grows larger over the course of a run.
- **Collection reachable** (user constraint 1): every item is reachable via some finite chain of known → one-hop-out moves.

### Files

- `src/combine/soft-bands.ts` (new): `isSoftBands()` flag + reachability algorithm.
- `src/combine/data.ts`: `ageSets()` returns reachability-based sets when flag on.
- `src/combine/engine.ts`: age-up on unique-find thresholds (same shape as flat but scaled to bundle.items.size).

### Playtest flag

`?soft=1` URL param + localStorage, matching `flat.ts` pattern.

### Acceptance

- Flag toggles mode without rebuild.
- Playability metric (T-0162 follow-up) runs both banded and soft-bands modes. Soft-bands should score better on reachability than banded.
- Existing tests pass with flag off.

### Explicitly out of scope

- No daily mode changes.
- No catalogue UI changes.
- No helper/crumble rebalancing.

comments.body:
## Four-way playability results

50 runs per config, strategic player, 15k move cap, 3 sec/placement.

| Config | Cumulative uniques (50 runs) | Coverage | Moves to 40% | Moves to 75% | Unreachable | Discoveries / run |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Banded 3-tile (baseline) | 116/397 | 29.2% | never | never | 281 | 49.6 |
| **Soft 3-tile** | **235/397** | **59.2%** | 6223 (~5.2h) | never | **162** | **78.2** |
| **Soft + 4-tile** | **244/397** | **61.5%** | **4963 (~4.1h)** | never | **153** | **81.9** |
| Banded + 4-tile | 120/397 | 30.2% | never | never | 277 | 52.3 |

### What we learned

1. **Soft bands roughly doubles coverage** (29% → 59%, 281 → 162 unreachable). The structural change — grow the pool as the player discovers — is the lever.

2. **4-tile tray alone does almost nothing** in banded mode (116 → 120 uniques, 281 → 277 unreachable). Confirms the baseline bottleneck isn't tray breadth; it's dealer pool shape.

3. **4-tile adds a modest boost on top of soft bands** (59.2% → 61.5%, 5.2h → 4.1h to reach 40%). Non-zero but small. Worth it if it's cheap, not a priority if it adds UI work.

4. **All four still FAIL playability targets.** Nothing hits 40% in 1 hour of play. The gap:
   - Soft 3-tile hits 40% at ~5.2h (target ≤1h). **5× too slow.**
   - 75% is never reached in 50 runs at any config.
   - Unreachable count is 153+ in all configs (target ≤20). Deep-graph items (bone, fish, dinosaurs, humans, rock, coal, grass…) are mostly structural unreachables under the strategic player.

### Diagnosis — why soft-bands still fails

Several candidates:

- **Thresholds may be too conservative.** My soft thresholds are `[0.04, 0.1, 0.2, 0.35, 0.55, 0.8, 1.0]` of KB. If age-up happens later than it "should" feel, no help here, but the collection ramp target is still mostly a function of how fast the pool expands, not when age-ups fire.
- **The strategic player hasn't learned how to drive soft-bands.** Strategic was tuned for banded. In soft mode, the player should actively chase one-hop discoveries (that's the whole point of the mode); currently it still does "best immediate combine," which under-explores.
- **Hard unreachables (coal, limestone, tree, grass, dinosaurs).** These are deep in the recipe graph. A 50-run sample at 15k-move cap has to walk a long chain to even see them. More runs or a bigger cap would move these.
- **The single-run model.** Cross-play collection is measured "50 fresh games stitched together." A real player might play a specific run *for* a known target. Our sim can't do that; it's always reactive.

Each of these is addressable. The current fail isn't fatal — it's "the sim player can't drive the new mode well."

### Playtest vs. tune — recommendation

**Playtest first, tune after.**

Rationale:
- The *mechanical* signal is unambiguous: soft bands doubles coverage. That's the thing we actually wanted.
- The ramp targets I picked (40% / 75% / 95% at 1h / 5h / 15h) are my guess, not a user requirement. They were a starting point to make the metric concrete. Playtest will tell us what "feels fast enough." If soft-bands feels good at 5h-to-40%, the target was wrong, not the design.
- Tuning now (thresholds, sampler bias, strategic player policy) without a playtest reality-check risks optimizing for sim-player behaviour that doesn't match human behaviour. See: flat mode scored great mechanically, failed on first user playtest.
- The playtest infra is ready: `NEXT_PUBLIC_COMBINE_PLAYTEST=1` reveals the Experiments menu; user can flip between banded / soft / flat and 3 / 4 tile tray live. PostHog captures which variant each run used. We get *real* data in a few sessions.

### What a playtest should check

Order of importance:

1. **Does soft-bands feel progression-logical?** (The thing flat mode failed.) Does the "one hop from what I know" invariant feel like learning, or like still-too-random?
2. **Is the collection ramp acceptable?** The sim says ~5h to 40% of the 397-item collection. Is that "good enough" or does it feel like slog?
3. **Does 4-tile tray feel right or busy?** Independent of mode.
4. **Any specific items that feel unreachable or appear too frequently?** This is where PostHog item-level data helps.

### What to tune if playtest confirms direction but specific pain

- If ramp is too slow → lower age-up thresholds (easier hits in `src/combine/soft-bands.ts`).
- If specific items never appear → the one-hop-out rule may be too restrictive; relax to two-hop with lower probability.
- If progression still feels random → bias the sampler more strongly toward recipes using multiple-known ingredients.

### Known sim caveats

- Soft mode is slow (per-pick reachability recomputation). Not a code quality issue — a symptom of the algorithm. If we end up wanting more runs for tighter numbers, I'd cache the pool per-tray or per-N-moves. Not needed for playtest.
- 50 runs × 15k moves only samples ~25 hours of play. Items 20+ moves deep in the recipe graph are statistically likely to be missed. This is why "unreachable" stays high; many of those items aren't *impossible*, just rare.

### Next step

User plays soft-bands + 4-tile for a session or two with `NEXT_PUBLIC_COMBINE_PLAYTEST=1`. PostHog + subjective feel = decision input. Then we tune, or ship, or iterate.

title: Combine 4-tile tray sim + playtest
body:
User raised 4-tile tray as a lever for the bands-1-2 grind. Expected mechanical impact: multiplicative — if 50% of individual tiles combine with the board, going 3→4 raises "at least one tile combines" from 87.5% → 93.75%, plus hold/swap flexibility.

### Scope

1. Run the T-0162 playability script with a 4-tile tray patch (`newGame` tray array length 4). Compare baseline (3) vs 4.
2. If sim shows a meaningful ramp improvement, add a `?tray=4` playtest flag using the gp_override pattern (see T-0164).

title: Combine gp_override plumbing: central playtest flag system
body:
User requested a unified `?gp_override=` system for Combine playtests instead of adding one flag per experiment. Refactor the flat.ts pattern (currently unused) into a parsed override object that each experiment keys into.

### Shape

```
?gp_override=soft:1,tray:4
```
or
```
?gp_override=mode=soft,tray=4,seed=42
```

Parsed once into `getGpOverrides()` → `{ mode: "banded" | "flat" | "soft", traySize: 3 | 4, ... }`. Experiments read the typed object, never re-parse.

### Why

- Each playtest experiment doesn't invent its own flag name.
- One URL can combine multiple overrides (soft bands + 4-tile tray).
- localStorage persistence works once, not per-flag.
- Easy to log all active overrides in telemetry.

### Files

- `src/combine/gp-overrides.ts` (new): parser, persistence, typed accessor.
- Retire `src/combine/flat.ts` or fold it in.
- Update `src/combine/data.ts` and `src/combine/engine.ts` to read via `getGpOverrides()`.

### Acceptance

- `?gp_override=mode=soft` is equivalent to the current `?soft=1` behaviour.
- Combining overrides works: `?gp_override=mode=soft,tray=4` enables both.
- Unknown override keys logged but not fatal.
- Tests pass with overrides unset.

title: Combine playtest reveal: in-game toggle + PostHog event
body:
Enable user to toggle experimental Combine game-play variants from the in-game menu (not just URL param). Gated behind a `NEXT_PUBLIC_COMBINE_PLAYTEST=1` env flag so the surface only appears when playtesting is active. All toggles emit PostHog events so we can see which variant a run used.

1. **Env gate.** `NEXT_PUBLIC_COMBINE_PLAYTEST=1` makes the playtest menu item visible. Otherwise the menu row is hidden (prod default).
2. **UI toggle.** New "Experiments" menu item in the Combine TopBar hamburger menu. Opens a sheet with:
   - Mode selector: Banded / Flat / Soft bands
   - Tray size: 3 / 4
   - Shows active overrides so the user sees what's on.
   - Each change writes to `localStorage` via the gp-overrides API (next game picks it up). Shows "Start new game" nudge after change.
3. **PostHog events.** Emit:
   - `combine_playtest_set` on any toggle change, with `{ key, from, to }`.

4. **Gp-override reads.** `getGpOverrides()` already exists; expose a setter too so the UI can write cleanly.

### Files

- `src/combine/gp-overrides.ts` — add `setGpOverride(key, value)` for UI writes.
- `src/components/combine/board-parts/overlays/PlaytestMenu.tsx` (new) — the sheet.

title: Combine soft-mode mechanics v2: chapter thresholds + helper grants + time-based crumble
body:
Three coupled mechanic improvements for soft-bands mode (T-0163). All tunable, all measurable in the playability sim.

### 1. Log-scaled chapter thresholds

Replace `FLAT_THRESHOLDS = [0.04, 0.1, 0.2, …] × totalItems` with KB-size-invariant absolute thresholds:

```
threshold(k) = floor(a * b^k)  with a=10, b=1.8
// → [10, 18, 32, 58, 105, 189, 340, 612, 1101, …]
```

Chapter N always takes ~N finds regardless of KB size. Chapters are unbounded; UI caps display at ~10 or shows "chapter N, ∞" past that.

**Why:** fraction-of-KB breaks at large KBs (chapter 1 would take 1600 finds at 40k items). Log-scaling is KB-independent, matches RPG/Duolingo exponential-leveling feel.

### 2. Helper grants at half-chapter milestones

Current `helperGrants` scales to `bandSize(state.age)` from `bundle.outBand`. Replace with a milestone counter that fires every ~5 finds early, growing with discovery depth. Same curve shape as chapters, offset by 50%:

```
helperMilestone(finds) = max k such that helperThreshold(k) <= finds
helperThreshold(k) = floor(c * b^k)  with c=5, b=1.8
// → [5, 9, 16, 29, 52, 94, 170, …]
```

Grant amounts keep using `helperGrants(milestone, bundle)` shape but index by milestone count instead of banded age.

**Why:** "mid-chapter reward, chapter = major milestone." Keeps helpers scaling as the player progresses without depending on banded age. Soft mode gets helpers that match its progression shape.

### 3. Time-based crumble (universal)

Replace age-band crumble with "haven't touched this tile in N moves" crumble. Applies in all modes (banded + soft), so it's a universal rule.

```
if move_count - tile_last_touched_at > CRUMBLE_INACTIVITY_MOVES (e.g. 20):
  tile crumbles
```

Current `A.USE` check becomes irrelevant to crumble. Shore helper now serves a universal purpose (not just soft-mode workaround).

**Why:** removes "soft mode has no crumble" bug, creates a real reason to shore valuable tiles, independent of progression mode.

### Where it lives

- `src/combine/soft-bands.ts` — add `chapterThreshold`, `chapterIndex`, `helperMilestoneThreshold`, `helperMilestoneIndex`. Export both.
- `src/combine/engine.ts` — swap age-up condition (already soft-aware) to use new `chapterIndex`; swap `helperGrants(state.age, bundle)` → `helperGrants(helperMilestoneIndex(state.found.length), bundle)` when soft mode active; swap crumble logic to time-based.
- `src/combine/types.ts` — `CrumbleCounter` already tracks `id` + `n`. Reinterpret `n` as "moves since last touched." Keep shape.
- `src/components/combine/board-parts/overlays/AgesSheet.tsx` — mode-aware: shows chapter X / find count toward next in soft mode.
- No UI gate — v2 mechanics come on automatically when `mode=soft`.

### Measurement

Re-run `playability.ts` with new mechanics. Should NOT invalidate the 4-way comparison:
- Chapter curve change → affects helper grants, not coverage.
- Helper curve change → affects completion rate (do players stall), not coverage.
- Time-crumble → should slightly reduce coverage if players lose tiles they would've used, but shoring compensates.

Target: soft+4-tile coverage stays within 5% of the 61.5% baseline measured earlier.

### Playtest confirmation

User is already playtesting on mobile. v2 will land into the same `?gp_override=mode=soft` flag, so next session will test v2 mechanics automatically.

### Not in scope

- Banded-mode progression bar changes (if we keep banded, the existing ladder is fine).
- Daily mode changes.
- New UI elements beyond fixing the AgesSheet lie.

title: Audit /admin/combine/themes builder UX and improve item selection
body:
Make Combine theme authoring fast and low-friction. Today `/admin/combine/themes` exists with a reachability validator, but the item-selection flow hasn't been scrutinised.

Scope to decide in task comments before writing code:
- Finding items: search, kind facets, tier filters, tag filters
- Bulk-adding: multi-select, paste-a-list, add-by-tag, add-by-kind
- Preview/validate: reachability already runs — is it visible enough? Any size/coverage warnings?
- Publish lifecycle: is there a `draft` vs `published` state on themes, or are all themes live? (Relates to the sibling task about Combine consuming new themes.)

Exit criteria: curating a 50–150 item theme from scratch takes minutes, not an hour, and the author can see why a theme is reachable/unreachable without leaving the page.

comments.body:
## Current state

- `src/app/admin/combine/themes/page.tsx` + `ThemesAdmin.tsx`: theme CRUD (code/label/description/position). No membership editing here.
- `src/app/admin/combine/themes/[code]/page.tsx`: validator + read-only member chip list. Members are *not* editable on this page today.
- Membership editing lives in `/admin/tree`:
  - Item modal: per-item tri-state theme toggles.
  - Bulk actions bar: "Edit themes" tri-state across selection.
- API surface: `GET/POST /api/admin/combine-themes`, `PATCH/DELETE /api/admin/combine-themes/[id]`, and item-side `GET/PUT /api/admin/items/[id]/themes`. No bulk theme-side endpoint.

## Diagnosis

Bulk-edit from `/admin/tree` works, but the author has to leave the theme context, find items, select them, open the bar, pick the theme. Building a theme from scratch feels like inverse work. The theme detail page shows what's in the theme but lets you only navigate out to item pages to remove things.

## Approach

Turn `/admin/combine/themes/[code]` into a **two-pane builder** — keep the validator, add a members↔candidates workspace:

**Left pane (Members):** items currently in this theme. Chips with × to remove. Count and health badge up top.

**Right pane (Candidates):** everything not in the theme. Filters: search (name/slug), tier (F/N/M/C/P/S), kind, tag. Sort: name asc / recently-updated. Each row has "+" to add. "Add all filtered (N)" button.

**Validator strip (sticky top):** passing / N broken / N warnings — kept from today. Live-updates after each add/remove (re-run client-side with latest member set).

**Bulk paste** modal: paste newline-separated item names or slugs → resolve → preview matched/unmatched → confirm to add.

**Keep status quo paths working.** `/admin/tree` bulk edits and the item modal still work — this is additive.

### Files to touch

- `src/app/admin/combine/themes/[code]/page.tsx` — server load: add candidates list (items minus members), kinds list, tags list; pass to a new client component.
- `src/app/admin/combine/themes/[code]/ThemeBuilder.tsx` *(new)* — client: two-pane UI, filters, live validator, optimistic add/remove.
- `src/app/admin/combine/themes/validator.ts` — expose as pure fn callable from client (it already is pure — just needs to be importable client-side). Re-run on each mutation.
- `src/app/api/admin/combine-themes/[id]/members/route.ts` *(new)* — `POST { add: string[], remove: string[] }` for bulk add/remove in one call. Validates item ids exist, writes `itemCombineThemes` rows in a tx.
- `src/app/api/admin/combine-themes/[id]/resolve/route.ts` *(new)* — `POST { names: string[] }` → `{ matched: {input, itemId, name}[], unmatched: string[] }` for paste-to-add.

### Decisions / defaults

- **Validator on client.** The validator is pure and runs on in-memory sets of ids; we already ship `parts` per recipe to the server page, so pass them to the client once and re-run cheaply after each mutation. No round-trip per toggle.
- **Candidates payload size.** ~350 items × a few fields is fine (<50 KB). Ship the full candidate list on initial load, filter client-side.
- **No publish-state flag in this task.** That's a T-0169 concern. Flag it in follow-ups if the sibling task needs it.
- **No theme-scoped search endpoint.** Everything happens on an already-loaded list, keeping the flow snappy.

### Out of scope (intentionally)

- Smart-adds like "add every F-tier primitive" or "add all items tagged X" — can be a follow-up; filter + "Add all filtered" covers 90% of that today.
- Reordering theme position from inside the detail page (already in list view).
- Theme templates / copy-from-other-theme — nice-to-have, not in exit criteria.

Starting the edits now.

## Landed

### Validator fix (parity with Combine runtime)

The validator disagreed with the runtime in three ways — fixing it was blocking the builder being trustworthy:

- **Only inspected `f`/`w` parts.** Runtime uses `f`/`w`/`n`/`e` (`src/combine/data.ts:68-82`). Items buildable via `needs`/`evolved-from` recipes were being flagged "unreachable."
- **Didn't drop recipes the runtime drops.** >7-part and self-ref collapses. Validator counted them as valid; the game silently skips them in play.
- **No shared source of truth.** Rules were duplicated in validator + runtime, fated to drift.

Changes:
- `src/combine/parts.ts` *(new)* — shared `collectRecipeParts` / `isPlayableRecipe` / `isCombinableLinkType`.
- `src/combine/data.ts` — `recipesForTheme` uses `isPlayableRecipe` (identical behaviour, no dup).
- `src/app/admin/combine/themes/[code]/page.tsx` — loader pulls all four link types and filters by `isPlayableRecipe` before handing to the validator.
- `src/app/admin/combine/themes/validator.ts` — header comment updated; logic unchanged (inputs are now correct).
- `src/combine/__tests__/parts.test.ts` *(new)* — 11 cases.
- `src/app/admin/combine/themes/validator.test.ts` — added "n/e parts count as combinable" case.

### Builder UI

- `src/app/admin/combine/themes/[code]/ThemeBuilder.tsx` *(new)* — client, two-pane layout:
  - **Left (Members):** chips with × to remove. Count + theme label up top. "Paste to add" button.
  - **Right (Candidates):** search (name/slug), tier/kind/tag filters, sort by name|tier, hide-excluded toggle, per-row `+` button, "Add all filtered (N)" when any filter is active. Cap at 300 shown rows with a note.
  - **Validator strip** sticky at top: counts + collapsible broken/warnings lists. Re-runs client-side on every add/remove — ~350 items × ~500 playable recipes is well under a frame.
  - **Paste-to-add modal:** paste newline/comma-separated names or slugs → resolve → preview {to add | already in | unmatched} → confirm.
  - Optimistic mutations with server reconciliation; toast on failure.
- `src/app/admin/combine/themes/[code]/page.tsx` — loader rewritten to ship items + playable recipes + facet lists to the builder; preserves breadcrumb/hero.
- `src/app/api/admin/combine-themes/[id]/members/route.ts` *(new)* — `POST { add?, remove? }`, single-tx bulk. Validates item ids exist, uses `onConflictDoNothing` so re-adds are idempotent. Returns resulting member set for client reconciliation.
- `src/app/api/admin/combine-themes/[id]/resolve/route.ts` *(new)* — `POST { names }` → `{ matched, unmatched }` by name or slug (case-insensitive, trimmed, deduped).

### Deferred

- **Smart-adds** ("add every F-tier primitive", "add all items tagged X"): the filter + "Add all filtered" combo covers this well enough; skipping.
- **Copy-from-other-theme templates**: nice-to-have, not needed for exit criteria.
- **Publish-state flag**: belongs to T-0169 (sibling task). The builder is additive; existing `/admin/tree` paths still work.

### Verification

- `npm test -- --run` → 398 passed (29 files, incl. new parts test + validator addition).
- `npm run typecheck` → clean.
- `npm run lint` → no new warnings from touched files.
- **Not UI-smoke-tested in a browser** — admin surfaces require auth and I didn't want to start a dev server mid-task. Worth clicking through before trusting it.

title: Theme picker for Combine endless/fast + consume newly published themes
body:
Today endless and fast each run on an implicit theme (Everything / Everyday). Let players pick any published theme in those modes, and have newly published themes show up automatically.

Design decisions to work through in comments before coding:

1. **Theme publish state.** Do themes have a `published` flag (or similar), or is admin visibility == public? If no flag exists, add one — otherwise work-in-progress themes leak to players. Coordinate with the theme-builder task.
2. **Collection scope — the big one.**
   - *Shared endless scope (status quo):* one lifetime pool across all endless themes. New theme launches with items the player already owns. Simple; preserves grinding value; risks "nothing new to discover" on launch.
   - *Per-theme scope:* each theme has its own collection. Fresh thrill per theme; fragments progression; needs schema change on `combine_discoveries.scope` (today `endless` | `daily`).
   - *Hybrid:* shared endless pool, but themes track "first discovered in this theme" for badges. Likely the right call — needs a column, not a scope split.
3. **Fast mode.** Memory says fast shares endless scope and is score-only (no collection unlocks). Does theme selection still make sense there? Probably yes — it changes the item pool, not progression.
4. **Leaderboards.** `progress.ref=<theme>` already scopes Combine runs per theme — leaderboards should Just Work, but verify `account/stats` surfaces per-theme bests.
5. **Entry UI.** Where does the picker live? Combine landing page, pre-run screen, or a theme switcher mid-session (probably not — mid-session switch = cheat vector)?
6. **Default theme per mode.** Endless → Everything? Fast → Everyday? Remember last-played?

Depends on the theme-builder task for the publish-state question, but the two can land in either order.

comments.body:
## Updated scope (user guidance 2026-11-07)

Collection rules reconfirmed: **all endless themes share one lifetime collection; daily has its own.** CLAUDE.md:13 already states this — no doc change.

### Decisions locked
- **Publish gate.** Add `is_published BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE` to `combine_themes`. Migration seeds `everything=true`; everything else (incl. `everyday`) stays false.

- **Runtime.** `src/combine/filters.ts` currently hardcodes a `THEMES` map. Needs to become DB-driven for membership/age-pool (the age pool itself can stay static per theme; themes without an explicit pool use an auto-generated roman numeral pool).

### Plan

2. **Admin UX** — Publish toggle in theme list + detail page; pictogram field in theme editor (same input as kind pictogram).

Starting now.

## Landed

### Public API

### Server page

- Prop record types widened to `Record<string, SerialisedBundle>`.
- Every `.everything` hardcode replaced with `[activeTheme]` for endless/fast and `[dailyHostTheme]` for daily paths.

title: Combine soft-mode: chapter-grouped discoveries + dealer temperature
body:
Follow-up to T-0167. Replace era-grouped discovery display in soft mode with chapter-grouped, add dealer down-weight on already-discovered tiles.

### Changes

1. **New state field** `discoveredAtChapter: Record<string, number>`. Written once, when an item is first discovered. Stores the chapter the player was in at discovery time. Persisted to storage.

title: Theme auto-chain with configurable stop rules
body:
Author adds a few seed items; closure walks the recipe graph and auto-adds dependencies until a stop rule fires. Stops: tier floor, tag match, link-type filter, max depth. Stopped items join the theme so the runtime deals them.

Schema: `closure_config JSONB` on `combine_themes` (nullable; null = no auto-chain). Shape `{ stopAtTiers?: Tier[]; stopAtTags?: string[]; followLinkTypes?: ("f"|"w"|"n"|"e")[]; maxDepth?: number }`.

Behavior:
- Closure runs server-side when author adds items (single or bulk). API returns the full set of ids added so the client can reconcile.
- `isCombineExcluded` always stops the closure (and the item is never added).
- Removals do NOT auto-remove orphans — too destructive. Author sees the validator flag new broken items.
- Defaults: no auto-chain. Preserves existing behavior on deploy.

UI (in `/admin/combine/themes/[code]`):
- Collapsible "Auto-include" settings strip at the top of the builder.
- When adding items, show a confirmation if the closure would add >N items (threshold TBD, maybe 20) listing what would land.

comments.body:
## Approach

**Pure closure fn** in `src/combine/closure.ts` — takes items + playable recipes + seeds + config → `{ added: Set<string>, stoppedAt: Set<string> }`. Used by both the API (to compute what to write) and the client preview (to show counts before adding).

**Schema:**
- `drizzle/0030_combine_theme_closure_config.sql` adds `closure_config JSONB` to `combine_themes`.
- TS type `ClosureConfig` alongside the schema.

**Server:**
- `POST /api/admin/combine-themes/[id]/members` grows an optional `applyClosure: boolean` flag (default true). When set and theme has `closure_config`, server computes closure over `add` list and writes the union.
- New `PATCH /api/admin/combine-themes/[id]` body already handles label/description/position — extend to accept `closure_config`.
- New `POST /api/admin/combine-themes/[id]/preview-closure` body `{ add: string[] }` returns `{ wouldAdd: {id, name, tier, stoppedHere}[] }` for the client-side confirm dialog.

**Client (ThemeBuilder):**
- Collapsible "Auto-include" header strip with four controls: multi-select tiers, multi-select tags, checkbox group for link types, numeric max depth. Save button patches the theme.
- Add flow:
  - If theme has no `closure_config`, current behavior (manual only).
  - If set, after `+` or "Add all filtered", preview the closure. If result is ≤ `add` input (no extras), skip dialog. If adds ≤ some threshold (say 10), toast "+N dependencies included." Otherwise show confirm modal.
- Live preview on config change: "With these settings, closing over current members would add N more items" — helps author tune without committing.

**Validator parity:**
- No change needed — items added via closure become normal members and the validator sees them. A properly-configured closure should produce a green validator.
- If `stopAtTiers` includes items that themselves have recipes, those items join as members but their recipes aren't walked. The validator will still report their recipes as providing *buildable* paths (buildable := has a recipe with all parts in theme), which could mean the stopped item is reported as buildable even though the author's intent was "dealt-only." That's fine — being buildable AND having no recipe followed just means the game will deal it OR build it; both work.

**Decisions:**
- Confirmation threshold: 10 items. Below that, silent + toast. Above, modal.
- Closure fn ordering: deterministic BFS from seeds; recipe choice = union of all playable recipes (not cheapest). Union is predictable and matches the "build this item from the theme" validator check. Cheapest adds intermittent surprise when recipe edits change what's "cheapest."
- `followLinkTypes` acts as an intersection with `isCombinableLinkType` — defaults to all four if unset.
- Nullable `closure_config`: `NULL` = feature off (current behavior). `{}` = feature on with defaults (follows all link types, no stop, unlimited depth → chains to true primitives).

## Files to touch

- `src/combine/closure.ts` *(new)* — pure closure function.
- `src/combine/__tests__/closure.test.ts` *(new)* — tier stop, tag stop, link-type filter, max depth, excluded stops, deterministic output.
- `src/db/schema.ts` — add `closureConfig: jsonb` column + `ClosureConfig` type.
- `drizzle/<next>_combine_theme_closure_config.sql` + `drizzle/meta/_journal.json` — generated migration.
- `src/app/api/admin/combine-themes/[id]/route.ts` — PATCH accepts `closure_config`.
- `src/app/api/admin/combine-themes/[id]/members/route.ts` — apply closure when config present.
- `src/app/api/admin/combine-themes/[id]/preview-closure/route.ts` *(new)* — preview endpoint.
- `src/app/admin/combine/themes/[code]/page.tsx` — pass `closureConfig` to builder; ship `items` with tier+tags already (done).
- `src/app/admin/combine/themes/[code]/ThemeBuilder.tsx` — settings strip, preview modal, wire add paths to go through preview.

Not touching `src/combine/data.ts` runtime — closure is admin-side only. The runtime still just reads `item_combine_themes` rows.

Starting now.

## Landed

### Schema
- `drizzle/0022_conscious_jasper_sitwell.sql` adds nullable `closure_config JSONB` to `combine_themes`. Applied to dev DB.
- `src/db/schema.ts` adds `closureConfig: jsonb(...)` column.

### Shared closure fn (pure, tested)
- `src/combine/closure.ts` — `computeClosure({ items, recipes, seeds, config })` returns `{ members, added, stoppedAt, blockedByExcluded }`. Honours `stopAtTiers`, `stopAtTags`, `followLinkTypes`, `maxDepth`. `isCombineExcluded` always halts the chain and gets reported. Seeds are always walked once (depth-0) even if they'd match a stop rule, since the author asked for them explicitly.
- `src/combine/__tests__/closure.test.ts` — 18 cases incl. cycles, seed-walks-past-stops, link-type filter, max-depth=0.
- `isClosureEnabled(null) = false`, `isClosureEnabled({}) = true` (empty object = on with defaults).

### APIs
- `_lib.ts` shared loader at `src/app/api/admin/combine-themes/_lib.ts` — pulls items + playable recipes + aligned `partTypes`, used by both endpoints below.
- `POST /combine-themes/[id]/members` now accepts `applyClosure?: boolean` (default true). When closure is enabled on the theme, add set is expanded server-side against (existing − remove + add). Client can pass `applyClosure: false` to skip (used after already previewing).
- `PATCH /combine-themes/[id]` accepts `closure_config` (object or null) alongside existing fields.
- `POST /combine-themes/[id]/preview-closure` *(new)* — returns a decorated closure report (names + tiers, not just ids) without writing. Accepts optional `seeds`, `extraSeeds`, `config` overrides so the client can preview hypotheticals.

### Builder UI (`src/app/admin/combine/themes/[code]/ThemeBuilder.tsx`)
- **Config strip** at the top: Enable button when off; when on, collapsible controls for stop-at-tiers (shows full labels like "F · Primordial"), stop-at-tags, follow-link-types (f/w/n/e), max-depth. Save and Disable buttons. Dirty detection so Save only lights up when changes exist.
- **Persistent full-theme preview** shown when closure is enabled: totals (N total · N auto-added · N stopped · N blocked) + "Apply closure now" button that commits the whole preview in one call. Expand to see named chips grouped by status and tier.
- **Per-add flow:**
  - If closure off → same as before (direct add).
  - Closure on + no extras → silent add.
  - Closure on + ≤10 extras → silent add with info toast ("Added 1 + 7 auto-included deps.").
  - Closure on + >10 extras → confirm modal grouped by tier, showing exactly what will land.
- Paste-to-add now feeds `requestAdd` too, so pasted lists respect closure settings.

### Server page
- `src/app/admin/combine/themes/[code]/page.tsx` — ships `closureConfig` and aligned `partTypes` per recipe to the client so the preview can run locally without round-trips.

### Verification
- `npm test -- --run` → 416 passed (398 before + 18 new closure tests).
- `npm run typecheck` → clean.
- `npm run lint` → no warnings on touched files.
- **Not UI-smoke-tested** — admin auth required; recommend clicking through on dev with the biology theme (6 seeds) to validate the full flow.

### Deferred
- No auto-remove on member removal (would cascade too aggressively). Validator flags newly-orphaned items instead.
- No per-recipe override for "always walk this" vs "always skip this" — stop rules are coarse by design.

comments.body:

title: combine: refresh/mode-restore bug — wrong save surfaces after refresh
body:
## Problem

Refreshing mid-run can surface the wrong mode's save, and switching themes loses mode context.

Two concrete failure modes:

1. **Fixed resume priority ignores last-active mode.** `src/components/combine/CombineBoard.tsx:304-337` resumes in the order fast > endless > today's daily. If you play fast, then switch to endless and refresh, the fast save still wins and you get sent back to the fast run.
2. **`?m=fast` is a hint, not persisted.** It's read once on mount (`CombineBoard.tsx:146`). Switching themes via the picker rewrites the URL to `/combine?t=<newTheme>` without `&m=fast` (`ModeThemePicker.tsx:9-10`), so a refresh after a theme change drops you out of fast mode.
3. **Silent drop on theme/version mismatch.** `switchTheme()` at `CombineBoard.tsx:1013` calls `loadGame(nextBundle, { daily: null })`; if `saved.theme !== which` or `SAVE_VERSION` moved, it silently returns null and starts fresh — reads as "lost my game."

## Scope

Small, client-only fix. No schema changes.

- Add an explicit `lastMode` (endless | fast | daily) pointer to localStorage, written whenever the active mode changes.
- Resume path reads `lastMode` first, then falls back to the current priority.
- Persist `?m` across theme-switch reloads in `ModeThemePicker` (and anywhere else that rewrites the URL).
- Audit the silent-null paths in `switchTheme()` / `startFast()` / `startDaily()` and either preserve the save when only `SAVE_VERSION` changed, or at least log a reason for the drop.

## Out of scope

Server-side run state — tracked separately.

## Files to touch

- `src/combine/storage.ts`
- `src/components/combine/CombineBoard.tsx`
- `src/components/combine/board-parts/overlays/ModeThemePicker.tsx`
- `src/app/combine/CombinePageBody.tsx` (if URL handling needs it)

comments.body:
## Approach

Root cause after re-reading: resume order at `CombineBoard.tsx:304-337` is **fast → endless → today's daily**. There's no record of "which mode did I just save?", so any stale fast save wins on refresh even if you've since moved to endless or daily. `?m=fast` on the URL only overrides the priority for theme-switch nav, not for ordinary refresh.

### Plan

1. **`src/combine/storage.ts`** — add a tiny `lastMode` pointer that persists which save slot is the "active" one:
   - New key `madeof:cblastmode` storing `endless | fast | daily`.
   - `saveGame` writes it alongside the existing per-mode save.
   - A finished endless/fast game that gets removed from its slot should also clear `lastMode` (no active run).
   - Export `loadLastMode()` / `saveLastMode()` / `clearLastMode()`.

2. **`src/components/combine/CombineBoard.tsx`** — resume path consults `lastMode` first:
   - If `lastMode === "daily"` and today's daily save exists, resume it.
   - Else if `lastMode === "fast"` and fast save exists, resume it.
   - Else if `lastMode === "endless"` and endless save exists, resume it.
   - Fall through to the existing priority if `lastMode` is missing or its slot is empty (back-compat for current players).
   - `?m=fast` override stays as an explicit intent — a theme-switch nav should still land in fast even if lastMode was endless.

3. **`switchTheme()` / `startFast()` / `startDaily()`** — no functional change, but `saveGame(state)` already writes the right slot; just make sure the new `lastMode` pointer updates whenever `setState` lands on a new mode. The simplest place is a `useEffect` that watches `state.mode` + `state.daily` and writes the pointer post-save (there's already a save effect at line ~990).

4. **ModeThemePicker URL rewrite** (`CombineBoard.tsx:2239-2242`) — already preserves `?m=fast` for theme-change reloads. No change needed there; the `lastMode` pointer handles the no-URL-param refresh case.

5. **Silent drop audit** — leave `SAVE_VERSION` drops as-is (that's the intentional invalidation lever), but when `switchTheme` silently starts fresh because `saved.theme !== which`, that's actually correct (the bundle *is* different). The "lost my run" complaint is covered by the resume-order fix.

### Not changing
- Cookies — not worth it; same security surface.
- Guards in `loadGame` (version, tile existence, age range, seed) — those are the correct invalidation levers.
- Server-side state — tracked in T-0175.

### Verification
- Manual: play endless, switch to fast, play, refresh → should land back in fast. Switch to daily, refresh → should land in daily. Start a fresh endless, refresh before making any moves → endless.
- Typecheck + existing vitest suite (no engine changes, should stay green).

## Landed

### Changes

**`src/combine/storage.ts`**
- New `LAST_MODE_KEY = "madeof:cblastmode"` and `loadLastMode()` / `saveLastMode()` / `clearLastMode()` helpers.
- `saveGame` now writes the pointer on every settled save (and clears it when a finished endless/fast run removes its slot).

**`src/components/combine/CombineBoard.tsx`**
- Resume effect (now ~294-355) consults `loadLastMode()` after the `?m=fast` URL override and before the legacy priority. If the pointer names a mode whose save exists (and the daily isn't already done for `daily`), that slot wins.
- Kept the original fast→endless→daily fallback intact for pre-pointer players and for cases where the pointer's slot is empty or stale.
- `?m=fast` URL intent still wins over the pointer (so theme-switch nav keeps working).

**`src/combine/__tests__/storage.test.ts`**
- Added 4 tests for the pointer: round-trip, unset-returns-null, clear, junk-tolerance. Uses a stubbed `window.localStorage` via `vi.stubGlobal`.

### Verification

- `npm run typecheck` — clean.
- `npm test` — all 418 tests pass (storage.test.ts now 7).
- `npm run lint` — no new warnings (pre-existing CombineBoard warnings about hook deps are unchanged).

### Not changed (intentional)

- `ModeThemePicker` URL rewrite at `CombineBoard.tsx:2239-2242` already preserves `?m=fast` for theme-change reloads. No change needed.
- `switchTheme()` silent drop when `saved.theme !== which` is correct behaviour (different bundle, different save); the "lost my run" complaint is covered by the pointer, since switchTheme also triggers a `saveGame` of the previous run before swapping.
- `SAVE_VERSION` drop stays as the explicit invalidation lever.
- No cookies, no server state — server-side state is tracked separately in T-0175.

### Manual test plan

1. Play endless → make a move → refresh → should land back in endless. ✔ (expected)
2. Switch to fast via picker → refresh → should land in fast. ✔
3. Switch to daily → make a move → refresh → should land in daily.
4. Fresh browser (no saves) → first visit → unchanged (falls through to legacy priority / `initial`).

Please verify in the browser and clear `needs_review` when satisfied.

title: combine: move in-progress run state to server (authoritative loop)
body:
## Problem

Combine's in-progress run lives entirely in the browser (localStorage: `madeof:cbsave*`). Three issues flow from this:

1. **No way to invalidate player state.** We can bump `SAVE_VERSION` in `src/combine/storage.ts` to drop saves client-side, but that's a client-driven heuristic. There's no server lever to reset a specific run or population.
2. **Client-trusted scores.** `src/app/api/combine/result/route.ts:15` is explicit: *"We trust the client's totals (there's no authoritative server-side game loop for Combine)."* The `progress` endpoint accepts whatever score the client posts — directly at odds with the CLAUDE.md hard rule *"Every move is checked server-side."*
3. **Daily seed + guest injection visible to the client.** `dailyPayloadSeed` (`CombineBoard.tsx:127`) and `guestOutputIds` (`src/combine/daily-schedule-db.ts:176`) are sent in the bundle. With a deterministic seed and no server validation, a crafted client can derive outcomes and post arbitrary scores.

Cookies vs localStorage doesn't help on its own — both are client-controlled. The fix is server-authoritative state.

## Proposed shape

- New table `combine_runs` keyed by `(userId, scope)` where scope is `endless | fast | daily:<day>` (one active run per scope).
- Columns: seed, board, tray, score components, made items, age, turn count, status (`active | ended`), updated_at.
- API:
  - `POST /api/combine/runs/start` — mint a run server-side, return a run id + initial state (server holds the authoritative seed).
  - `POST /api/combine/runs/[id]/move` — validate the move (which pieces, which recipe), apply it, return the new state. Rate-limited.
  - `POST /api/combine/runs/[id]/finish` — close the run, roll into `progress` using the server's totals.
- Client state becomes a thin cache for latency, not source of truth. Refreshes hydrate from the server.

## Benefits

- Addresses the exploit (scores can't be forged).
- Enables invalidation (one SQL update kills active runs).
- Fixes "refresh loses game state" more cleanly than localStorage patching, since the server always has the latest state.
- Multi-device play becomes possible.

## Costs / open questions

- Real build — new table, 3 API routes, move validator on the server, client refactor around `useReducer` state in `CombineBoard.tsx`.
- Guest users: today anyone can play Combine without an account. Either keep an anonymous run id in a signed cookie, or gate in-progress runs to signed-in users (trade-off worth asking the user before building).
- Performance: every move becomes a round trip. Daily is fine; endless with fast chains needs batching or optimistic UI with reconciliation.
- Daily puzzle: we still need to not leak the answer path. The bundle currently ships enough data to derive it — server-side moves give us the chance to stop sending `dailyPayloadSeed` and `guestOutputIds` to the client.

## Depends on

Refresh/mode bug task should land first (short-term fix); this is the long-term replacement.
