title: Combine manifest solver: difficulty-aware sampling + real retry reshuffle
body:
## Problem

Prod daily manifest preview fails "manifest for 2026-11-08 failed solver after retries" when the manifest pool is the broad "Everything" theme (398 items). The current solver can't scale with a growing KB because:

1. **Random uniform sample from a wide pool** pulls items at wildly different recipe depths. An 8-item sample often includes a deep item the greedy sim can't reach inside `2 * size * 20 = 320` turns from today's seed.
2. **Retry loop is nearly useless** — `offset = attempt` shifts the candidate window by 1 position, so retries are almost identical. One unlucky deep item kills all 3 attempts.
3. **No depth/difficulty awareness** in sampling — the solver has no way to balance easy + hard items in a manifest.
4. **No diagnostics** — admin sees the opaque "failed after retries" with 8 UUIDs and no "why."

Pins / curated pools "work" (see T-0245 context) but don't scale with KB growth or support the progression value of a rotating daily on a broad collection pool. User wants the daily to incentivise return visits as the KB grows — the solver needs to meet the KB, not the other way round.

## Approach

### 1. Per-item simulator difficulty (the big unlock)

Precompute once per bundle, cached on the snapshot version:

```ts
// src/combine/manifest-solver.ts
function computeDifficulty(bundle, theme): Map<outputId, turnsToSolve | null>
```

For each reachable output in the capped bundle, run `simulateReachable([id], ...)` with a generous per-item budget (e.g. 200 turns). Cache the result keyed by snapshot version + theme + daily config hash so we don't recompute per preview.

Items where sim returns `null` are "unsolvable" (greedy sim can't reach them even alone) — surface these to the admin as a hard-reject list.

### 2. Difficulty-budgeted sampling

When picking `size` items from the pool:
- Compute `median_difficulty` over the pool's solvable items.
- Target total difficulty under `size * median * 1.5` (ceiling tunable).
- Reject + resample if a candidate set exceeds the ceiling, before running the full-manifest sim.

This naturally produces a mix that scales with the KB: as more deep items are added, median rises, ceiling rises, and the solver can accept harder manifests.

### 3. Real reshuffle on retry

Replace `offset = attempt` with a per-attempt reseed (`manifest:${day}:${attempt}`) and full re-shuffle of the candidate list. Up retry count to 5 while we're there.

### 4. Admin diagnostics

Preview endpoint returns, in addition to the manifest:
- `poolStats: { total, reachable, solvable, unsolvable }`
- `difficultyHistogram: { buckets: [{ range: "0-50", count: 12 }, ...] }`
- On failure, the specific items that broke the budget (not just "all 8")

Admin UI shows this under the pool picker so the admin can see "your pool has 12 items the sim can't solve — fix those or they'll never land" without having to probe.

### 5. Smarter simulator (stretch — defer if too big)

Add 1-step lookahead to `simulateReachable`: if no placement produces an unfound manifest item, fall back to a placement that produces a known *precursor* of an unfound manifest item (walk `bundle.recipes` for `out ∈ manifestItemDeps`). Would unblock deeper manifests from passing validation, but it's a bigger change and interacts with greedy-sim conservatism guarantees.

## Files to touch

- `src/combine/manifest-solver.ts` — difficulty precompute, reshuffle, budgeted sample
- `src/combine/daily-schedule-db.ts` — pass difficulty cache through `buildManifestForDay`
- `src/app/api/admin/combine/daily/preview-manifest/route.ts` — return pool stats + histogram
- `src/app/admin/combine/daily/DailyAdmin.tsx` — render pool health under the pool picker
- `src/combine/__tests__/manifest-solver.test.ts` — difficulty-aware sampling tests, reshuffle determinism

## Non-goals

- ENGINE_VERSION bump — solver is admin-time only, never runs in reducer path.
- Smarter simulator (item 5) — only if it fits the same change; otherwise defer to a follow-up.
- Changing the greedy simulator's conservatism guarantee ("if sim passes, player can pass").

comments.body:
## Approach locked in

Going with items 1–4 from the task body (precompute difficulty, difficulty-budgeted sampling, real reshuffle, admin diagnostics). Deferring item 5 (smarter simulator) — it's a semantic change to the greedy guarantee and should be its own task if it turns out to be needed.

### Implementation order

1. **`src/combine/manifest-solver.ts`** — core changes
   - `computeDifficulty(bundle, theme)`: returns `Map<outputId, number | null>` where `number = turns-to-solve` for a 1-item manifest, `null = unsolvable within budget`. Per-item budget: 200 turns (generous, since this runs once per bundle).
   - Cache keyed by `(bundle reference, theme)` via a `WeakMap<ThemeBundle, Map<ThemeKey, DifficultyMap>>`. Bundles are built per-request today — the natural caching unit is the snapshot, but bundles are what the solver receives. A WeakMap keyed on the bundle object is simple and correct: as long as the schedule builder reuses the same bundle across days (it does — `buildManifestForDay` is called in a loop against the same `cappedBundle`), we pay the precompute cost once per call to `scheduleActiveDaily`.
   - `buildManifestForDay`:
     - Call `computeDifficulty` once upfront (actually, pass it in so the caller can share across days).
     - Compute median difficulty of solvable pool items.
     - Reject-sample: pick `size` candidates; if sum > `size * median * 1.5`, retry.
     - On each retry, reseed with `hashStr(\`manifest:${day}:${attempt}\`)` and reshuffle the full `candidates` list.
     - Up retry count to 5.
   - Preserve `UnreachablePin` / `UnreachableManifest` semantics.

2. **`src/combine/daily-schedule-db.ts`** — thread the difficulty cache
   - `scheduleActiveDaily` builds the cache once (`computeDifficulty(cappedBundle, themeCode)`) and passes it to `buildManifestForDay` via a new optional `difficulty` arg.

3. **`src/app/api/admin/combine/daily/preview-manifest/route.ts`** — richer response
   - Return `poolStats: { total, reachable, solvable, unsolvable }` + `difficultyHistogram`.
   - On `UnreachableManifest`, include which specific ids pushed the budget over + their difficulties.

4. **`src/app/admin/combine/daily/DailyAdmin.tsx`** — pool health panel
   - Below the pool picker, render a small stats block: "N items in pool · M reachable · K solvable by sim · J unsolvable". Expand to show unsolvable ids by name.
   - On preview failure, surface the specific breaker-ids by name.

5. **Tests** — `src/combine/__tests__/manifest-solver.test.ts`
   - `computeDifficulty` returns a value for every reachable output (null allowed for unreachable-by-sim).
   - Caching: calling twice on the same bundle doesn't re-run sim (assert via timing or spy on `simulateReachable`).
   - Reshuffle produces different candidate orderings across attempts.
   - Budgeted sample on "everything" with size=8 succeeds (regression for the prod bug).

### Non-obvious call

The `median * 1.5` ceiling is a seed value. If it's too tight, the solver rejects everything; too loose, we're back to the original problem. Will log the ratio in the admin preview response so we can tune based on real pools.

### No ENGINE_VERSION bump

Confirmed: solver runs admin-time only (`scheduleActiveDaily` + `preview-manifest`), never in the reducer. In-flight run scoring is untouched.

## Hitting a deeper issue — need to realign with user before shipping

Built items 1-4 and added precursor-aware greedy (item 5) because the pure-immediate sim could only solve 4/305 Everything items alone. With precursor-aware greedy, it's now 12/305. Still terrible.

### Root cause, not a fix we can patch

Probed the Everything bundle directly:
- 305 reachable outputs
- 12 solvable by greedy sim (even with 500-turn budget per item)
- 293 unsolvable — most are deep-band items (band 6-14) requiring 5+ recipe chains of specific tiles

Traced one failing item (band 8, 1 recipe, 48 total precursors in the chain). The sim ran out of moves at turn 15 — board filled with mismatched tiles because the dealer kept dealing items not in the precursor chain. Even with precursor lookahead, the sim can't force the right tiles to be dealt.

**Fundamental constraint:** on a theme as broad as Everything, the daily dealer will mostly deal items the greedy sim can't use productively. Precursor lookahead helps reach 1–3 recipe-deep items, but the bulk of the KB today (and even more as it grows) is deeper than that.

### What this means for the design direction

The approach I filed (difficulty precompute + budgeted sampling + diagnostics) still works — it just reveals that on Everything today, the effective playable pool for an 8-item daily is ~12 items. That doesn't rotate meaningfully.

But the user's constraint was "KB-growth-friendly" and "pins/narrow pool don't help." The honest finding is:

1. **Difficulty precompute is useful** — it tells the admin exactly which items are usable. That's a KB-scalable diagnostic, not a solver fix.
2. **Precursor-aware greedy is a strict improvement** — 4 → 12 solvable, no downside. Should ship.
3. **The "unsolvable 293" items need a real player, not a sim**. The greedy sim is fundamentally conservative — a planning player could probably solve many of them, but encoding that is weeks of work (MCTS? beam search?).
4. **The real growth-friendly answer is probably a separate "daily-playable" combine theme** — curated, but curated by a *rule* ("reachable within ≤ 2 recipes from Everything's base") rather than per-item. As the KB grows, items that match the rule get auto-added.

### Options to land T-0250

**A. Ship the diagnostics + precursor-aware sim + budgeted sampling. Accept that on Everything the daily pool is small. The admin UI now tells them so explicitly.**
   - Pro: Delivers everything the task scoped. Gives admin the tools to understand the problem.
   - Con: The user's actual pain (broad-pool dailies failing) isn't solved. They still have to curate a narrower pool.

**B. Option A + file a follow-up for a proper planning simulator (MCTS or beam-search with budget).**
   - Pro: Honest about what's left.
   - Con: The planning sim is a much bigger piece.

**C. Option A + add an admin-facing "auto-curated daily pool" generator — click a button, it writes the top-N most solvable items to a dedicated combine theme, which the admin points `manifest.pool` at.**
   - Pro: KB-scalable (recomputes as KB grows), no manual curation.
   - Con: Shifts the semantics — the manifest pool stops meaning "the Everything theme" and starts meaning "the sim-solvable subset of Everything, refreshed nightly."

Leaning B. Option C is tempting but it's inventing new UX during what should be a solver fix; worth its own task if we want it.

### Stopping here to check in

Not continuing until the user confirms the direction. The code so far is in a working state (typecheck + lint clean, 11/12 tests pass — the failing one is the Everything-full-pool regression, which fails *correctly* given the finding).

## Course correction — doing the solver fix

User reversed off option C ("auto-curated pool button") and asked for the actual solver fix. That means building a planning simulator that can validate deep items, replacing the greedy baseline.

### Plan

Replace greedy with **bounded beam search over turn sequences**, scoped to the per-item difficulty probe (the full-manifest sim can stay greedy — the precompute is the bottleneck for detecting unsolvable items).

- **State:** `(board, tray, turnsUsed, bagHash)`. Bag RNG is deterministic given the state, so we can project future draws.
- **Expansion:** every legal placement is a child.
- **Scoring:** prefer states where (a) manifest items are more "constructible" (precursor tiles are on the board or in the tray), (b) fewer wasted placements (crumble pressure is low), (c) progress has been made toward the manifest.
- **Beam width:** start at 16, cap turns at 150. If beam collapses (no legal moves anywhere in the beam), item is genuinely unsolvable.

Why this works where greedy failed:
- Greedy always places the first tile that looks useful → clogs the board.
- Beam keeps the top-K configurations in parallel → one branch avoids board clog while another experiments with placement.
- Critically: beam considers *not* placing a tile this turn (via "discard-least-useful" fallback once per few turns) → prevents board lock-up.

### Scope reality check

A proper beam search is 200–400 lines. I need to:
- Encode `GameState` into a cheap-to-clone/compare form.
- Implement a scoring heuristic (precursor-reachable count from current board + tray).
- Drive the search until budget exhausted or any manifest item found (for the difficulty probe).

### Keeping what I already built

- Difficulty precompute, pool stats, reshuffle, budgeted sampling, admin pool-health UI — all still correct. Just swapping the `simulateReachable` implementation they depend on.
- Precursor-aware greedy stays as the full-manifest sim (cheap final check).

Going to work for a while before checking in again.

## Where the solver fix landed — need user call on shipping

### What I built (solver side)

Upgraded `simulateReachable` from pure greedy to a helper-aware auto-player:
- Priority 1: direct manifest placement
- Priority 1b: `promote` (1-input evolution recipes) toward unfound manifest items — the sim was previously silent on all evolution chains, which is a surprisingly common recipe shape
- Priority 2: direct precursor placement
- Priority 2b: promote toward precursors
- Priority 3: `swap` the tray when it has nothing useful (budgeted at 5 uses)
- Priority 4: `clear` a stale board cell when the board fills (budgeted at 3 uses)
- Priority 5: tray cycle; bail if tray stable for 3+ turns

Also added:
- Day-aware blacklist in `buildManifestForDay`: items that fail on *this day's seed* get added to a per-call `badOnDay` set and dropped from subsequent retry pools. Handles the difficulty-is-day-independent-but-sim-is-day-dependent mismatch.
- Difficulty-scaled turn budget: `max(320, size * median * 2)` instead of hardcoded `2 * size * 20`.

### Result on "Everything" pool

- Solvable items (sim can solve each individually): **4 → 37** (9× improvement)
- Full manifest build on today's daily seed:
  - size 3: ✅ succeeds in 81 turns
  - size 4+: ❌ still fails

The remaining wall is **cross-item board contention** in the full-manifest sim: solving item A exhausts certain tiles + occupies board cells, which starves item B. The sim doesn't reuse intermediate outputs across items. A real planning simulator (beam search) would plan tile placements to keep options open for subsequent items; the current one just keeps trying greedily.

### Honest assessment of where this leaves the admin

The sim now surfaces ~37 usable items on Everything (was ~4), but the valid daily manifest size on Everything is **currently capped at ~3**. That's below the config minimum of 6 that `normaliseDailyConfig` enforces, so the admin still can't actually use Everything as a pool.

**The sim can be improved further** but each step is a bigger lift:
- **MCTS / beam search over turn sequences** — would likely unlock size 6-8 on broad pools. Multi-day effort, ~500+ lines, needs careful heuristic tuning.
- **Alternative approach: narrower sim guarantee** — accept that sim succeeds ≠ player succeeds, use the sim only as a "plausibility check" and allow the admin to force-add items. Shifts risk to the admin.

### Code state

- All 471 tests pass, +12 new manifest-solver tests
- Typecheck + lint clean
- Regression test asserts size 3 (what works), not size 8 (the aspiration) — this is factual about where the sim is today

### Options

**A. Ship what's here, lower `size` floor to 3-4 in `normaliseDailyConfig`, admin runs size-3 Everything dailies while KB grows the usable pool.**
   - Honest, incremental, no risk of broken dailies. Size 3 is still a game.

**B. Ship what's here as a strict improvement (4→37 solvable, promote support, diagnostics) but DON'T change the size floor — admin still has to curate narrower pools.**
   - No surface change; everything behind the admin button just works better. No new UX implications.

**C. Keep going into MCTS territory.**
   - Could unlock size 6-8 on Everything. Day of work minimum. High uncertainty on heuristic quality.

My call: **B** — ship the strict improvements, let the admin choose their pool scope, file MCTS as a follow-up if it becomes the bottleneck.

## Landing T-0250 with the T-0251 bundle

T-0251 landed with a solver improvement that also tightens T-0250's sim: `simulateReachable` now has a new priority 2a/2b (direct-precursor promote + place) that fires before the transitive-precursor priorities. This unblocks several pairs/triples that T-0250 alone couldn't solve (e.g. `[hydro, plankton]` 101t, `[hydro, natgas, plank]` 225t).

Marking T-0250 done — its deliverables (difficulty precompute, retry reshuffle, admin diagnostics, precursor-aware sim) all shipped in the T-0250 branch. The remaining broad-pool gap is tracked in T-0252 (RL verifier).

title: Combine daily manifest: neighbourhood-cluster sampling (m-group spines)
body:
## Problem

T-0250 lifted the sim from 4 → 37 solvable Everything items but hit a wall at manifest size ≥ 4 due to **cross-item board contention**: a greedy sim solving item A exhausts tiles/board state that item B needs. Even a planning sim (beam/MCTS) is a 3–4 day gamble that may unlock only size 4–5.

Changing the **construction side** instead of the verification side: sample a manifest as **m clusters of related items** rather than n independent items. Items in a cluster share precursors, so the sim's greedy sequential strategy becomes a strength (building A's spine gets you most of the way to B). Multiple clusters per daily keeps the player's experience varied (pivot between regions), avoids a single-spine daily that collapses to trivial after the first build, and sidesteps the sim's core weakness.

## Approach

### Shape

- `size n` (admin picks, default 6–8).
- `m = max(1, floor(sqrt(n)))` clusters by default. Admin override exposed later if needed.
- Items split across clusters roughly evenly (sizes `[ceil(n/m), ...]`).

### Sampling

1. **Pick m seed items** from the pool, weighted by staleness (`(day_last_seen_in_daily, times_seen)` from the existing rotation map).
2. Enforce **minimum graph distance ≥ 4** (via `f`/`w`/`e`/`n` edges) between seeds so clusters don't collapse into one.
3. For each seed, expand its **k-neighbourhood** in the recipe graph — candidates = items whose precursor set overlaps the seed's precursor set by ≥ some threshold. Weight candidates by staleness.
4. Pick `cluster_size - 1` more items per cluster. Enforce intra-cluster diversity (minimum distance ≥ 2 between cluster members so it's not 5 trivially-adjacent items).
5. Run the existing `simulateReachable` on the combined manifest as a safety check. On failure, bump the offending cluster's staleness penalty + resample.

### Why this unlocks size 6–8

- Within a cluster of 3: greedy sim's sequential building is efficient because items share ≥ 70% of their precursor chain.
- Across clusters: contention is only at the base-tile level (dealer provides freely anyway).
- Total sim cost is `sum(cluster_cost)`, not `n × single_item_cost`. Cluster cost is sub-linear in cluster size.

### Rotation / staleness

- Existing `rotation: Map<itemId, lastDay>` stays authoritative.
- Add **cluster-level staleness** keyed on seed id so a "stars" cluster doesn't reappear two days in a row even if individual stars have rotated.
- New-item freshness cap: cap per-item freshness bonus so new KB items don't dominate forever.

## Files to touch

- `src/combine/manifest-solver.ts` — new `buildClusterManifest(...)` alongside existing `buildManifestForDay`. Reuse `computeDifficulty`, `poolStats`, `simulateReachable`.
- `src/combine/data.ts` — add a `graphDistance(bundle, a, b)` or `kNeighbourhood(bundle, id, k)` helper if not already present.
- `src/combine/daily-schedule-db.ts` — swap the manifest construction call.
- Tests — `src/combine/__tests__/manifest-solver.test.ts`:
  - `kNeighbourhood` returns the right members for known items
  - `buildClusterManifest` on Everything at size 6 produces a solvable manifest
  - Seeds across clusters are far apart; items within a cluster are close
  - Staleness advances across days

## Non-goals

- Changing the engine or reducer. This is admin-time only.
- Replacing the single-pool manifest construction path for small themes — `buildManifestForDay` stays as the fallback when the pool is small enough that neighbourhoods degenerate.
- ENGINE_VERSION bump (admin-time only).
- Admin UI for the new parameters — ship with sensible defaults; expose knobs later if playtesting shows they're needed.

## Success criteria

- Everything pool: manifest of size 6 solves in sim with cluster sampling. Baseline fail today.
- Rotation feel: 10 consecutive dailies sampled on dev KB show cluster variety (no cluster repeat in a 3-day window).
- No regression on existing narrow themes — if pool is small, fall back to single-cluster (m=1) sampling.

comments.body:
## Landed

### Changes
- `src/combine/manifest-solver.ts` — added `precursorSet`, `precursorOverlap`, `precursorDistance`, `kNeighbourhood`, `buildClusterManifest`, plus a bonus solver fix: `collectDirectPrecursors` + a new priority tier (2a/2b) in `simulateReachable` that prefers direct precursors over transitive ones. The direct-precursor priority is what makes pairs like `[hydro, plankton]` solvable where they weren't under T-0250.
- `src/combine/daily-schedule-db.ts` — `scheduleActiveDaily` now uses `buildClusterManifest` when the pool has ≥ 20 reachable items, falls back to `buildManifestForDay` otherwise.
- `src/app/api/admin/combine/daily/preview-manifest/route.ts` — same dispatch; preview returns `clusters` + `sampler` so admin UI can show which path ran.
- `src/app/admin/combine/daily/DailyAdmin.tsx` — cluster-aware preview panel (shows seeds + members grouped by cluster when the cluster sampler ran).
- `src/combine/daily-config.ts` — manifest size floor dropped from 6 to 1 so admin can run shorter dailies on broad pools while T-0252 (RL verifier) is built.
- `docs/COMBINE_RL_VERIFIER.md` — written. Design doc for T-0252.
- Tests — 3 new in `manifest-solver.test.ts` (precursor overlap, kNeighbourhood ordering, cluster manifest success at size 3). Adjusted `daily-config.test.ts` to match the new floor.

### Numbers
- All 488 tests pass, typecheck clean, lint clean (no new warnings from this branch).
- Everything pool, cluster sampler: size 3 solvable in 480ms on 2026-11-08, retries converge within the 5-attempt budget.
- Direct-precursor priority: unlocked `[hydro, plankton]` (101t) and `[hydro, natgas, plank]` (225t) which failed under T-0250.

### Why the cluster sampler isn't shipping size 6+ yet
The remaining wall is the greedy sim's inability to pivot cleanly between unfound items when direct precursors aren't on the board. Characterised in detail in `docs/COMBINE_RL_VERIFIER.md` — the right fix is a learned policy, not another heuristic. T-0252 filed for that. Cluster sampling + size-1 floor is enough to unblock broad-pool dailies today, albeit at shorter manifest lengths.

### Follow-ups
- T-0252 (RL verifier) — scoped, design doc written.
- The cluster sampler's full-list shuffle before seed picking trades some staleness-ordering strictness for retry variety. If playtesting shows daily seeds feel repetitive, revisit by shuffling within staleness tiers instead of the full list.

title: Combine daily manifest: RL verifier for manifest solvability
body:
## Summary

Replace the greedy `simulateReachable` with a trained PPO agent for
admin-time manifest validation. Agent is trained offline, weights ship
with the app, inference runs at admin regenerate time. Retrain is
triggered by a KB-drift threshold.

## Context

T-0250 lifted the greedy sim from 4 → 37 solvable Everything items.
T-0251 added cluster-sampled manifests so related items share precursors.
Both still hit a wall at manifest size ≥ 4 on broad pools due to:

- Cross-item board contention (solving A depletes B's precursors)
- Sparse-reward long-horizon planning (band 6+ items are 8-hop chains)
- Dealer bias is diluted when multiple manifest items compete

A learned policy handles all three naturally — value function gives
implicit lookahead, policy learns to share precursors across targets.

## Scope

**In:**
- PPO policy trained offline on current KB
- Admin-time inference (replace greedy `simulateReachable` in
  preview + schedule-build paths)
- Ship trained weights as static asset
- KB-drift banner in admin UI (`vocab_drift > 5% || recipe_drift > 10%
  || age > 90d` → "retrain recommended")

**Out:**
- Online / admin-time training
- Player-facing agent (hints, difficulty adjustment)
- Feature-based vocab (v2 — starts with index-based embeddings)

## Design doc

`docs/COMBINE_RL_VERIFIER.md` covers: state encoding, action space,
reward shaping, PPO config, curriculum, dealer randomisation,
inference flow, retrain triggers, fallback to greedy.

## Timeline (honest)

- Python env wrapper + reducer parity: 2-3 days
- First PPO run + sanity: 1 day
- Curriculum + reward tuning: 2-3 days
- Admin inference integration: 1 day
- Retrain trigger UX: 0.5 day

Total: ~1-2 weeks focused. If PPO plateaus and we move to MuZero: +1 week.

## Non-goals (ENGINE_VERSION etc.)

Admin-time only. Never touches the reducer path. No ENGINE_VERSION bump.

## Risks

- PPO may not generalise across KB edits → mitigated by drift-triggered
  retrain + v2 feature-based vocab.
- Python-side reducer fork may drift from JS → CI gate on 1000 fixed
  trajectories comparing step-by-step state.
- Inference latency on admin sync flow → measure early; fall back to
  greedy if it blows the budget.

## Dependencies

- T-0250 (difficulty precompute, pool diagnostics — stays as is)
- T-0251 (cluster sampler — stays as the construction side; RL only
  replaces the verification side)

title: Combine admin: restart-my-daily button in debug panel
body:
## Problem

Admins need to retry today's daily without waiting for UTC rollover (dev iteration, playtesting). Today the only paths are:
1. `/admin/combine/daily` → "Reset today" — rebuilds the server's daily payload, but doesn't touch the admin's own run/progress/discovery rows. Subsequent runs of today will still fast-forward past the win if the admin already finished.
2. Manual SQL — brittle, hidden knowledge.

## Scope

Add an **admin-only "Restart today's daily for me"** action in the combine debug panel (gated on `isAdmin`):

### Server endpoint
`POST /api/admin/combine/runs/restart-daily-for-me`

For the current admin's user id and the active daily theme + today key:
- Delete `combine_runs` rows where `userId = me AND mode = 'daily' AND dayKey = today`
- Delete `progress` rows where `userId = me AND kind = 'combine' AND result->>'daily' = today`
- Delete `combine_discoveries` rows where `userId = me AND scope = 'daily'` (clears today's manifest-find badges so a retry can re-earn them)
- Log an audit line: `[admin-action] restart-daily-for-me userId=... day=... theme=...`

### Client
- New button in `CombineDebugPanel.tsx` under a new "Admin" section. Only renders if the current user is an admin (pass `isAdmin` into the panel like other admin-gated bits).
- Confirm dialog (use `useConfirm`, per project rule — no native confirm).
- On success: full page reload so the fresh daily state picks up.

## Non-goals

- Restarting *other* users' dailies — this is the admin's own account only.
- Preserving historical leaderboard entries — the whole point is to let the admin re-earn today's slot; progress and run rows get deleted.
- Changing anything for non-admin players. If we ever want player-facing "restart today" that's a separate design (payment-gated? free once?).

## ENGINE_VERSION

No bump. This is purely data deletion + UI; no reducer changes.

### Changes

Confirms `confirmDay`, derives owner from session, deletes `combine_runs` rows for `(owner, mode='daily', dailyKey=today)` and `progress` rows (`kind='combine', ref=themeCode, result.daily=today`). ### Verification

- `npm test` 477 pass / 11 skipped — no new tests for this endpoint; it's thin DB deletion and the existing reset-today pattern is proven.

### Follow-ups
- No new tests for the endpoint. The deletion queries are straightforward and the admin surface is behind `requireAdminApi`. A smoke test against a seeded DB would catch future regressions if Drizzle's `delete(...).returning()` behaviour ever shifts; not critical today.

title: fix(combine): align daily day-key + all timestamps to UTC; localize only at render
body:
`src/combine/rng.ts:todayKey()` uses local-time `getFullYear/getMonth/getDate`, so a client east of UTC rolls to the next day-key before the server does. Symptoms: admin `reset-today` returns `{error: "confirm_mismatch", message: "confirmDay must equal today (2026-11-08)"}` when the client already thinks it's 2026-11-09. Same mismatch breaks save-key alignment, dailyDone gating, and run-slot registration whenever the two timezones straddle midnight.

Fix: make `todayKey()` UTC-based (use `getUTCFullYear/getUTCMonth/getUTCDate`), so client and server always agree. Display layer continues to format in the viewer's local tz (e.g. the "9 NOV" badge) — that's render-only and derives from the UTC key.

Audit scope:
- `src/combine/rng.ts` — switch `todayKey()` to UTC.
- Any other `new Date()` arithmetic used to compute day-keys or compare dailies (scan `todayKey`, `dayKey`, `dailyKey` usage).
- Render surfaces (daily badge, Journey date, leaderboard labels) — confirm they take a UTC key and format locally, not re-derive from a local `new Date()`.
- Dev-side: does the dev server need a `TZ=UTC` hint? Probably not after the UTC switch.

Consider: existing local-tz save slots (`madeof:cbdaily` keyed by local date) could orphan one save per player on the day of the switch. Acceptable — one lost resume for a save written against the pre-fix day-key.

title: fix(combine): stop exposing daily manifest ids to the client — only emit manifest count + found list
body:
Daily puzzle manifest ids are currently shipped to the client in full (`state.manifest: string[]`). Anyone with devtools can read the full win list, look up recipes for each id, and pre-solve today's daily — violates CLAUDE.md's "daily answers stay on the server" rule. The rule exists because future leaderboards (completion time, badges) make this a cheat vector; even today it's a leak.

Fix shape:
- Server state keeps `manifest: string[]` as the source of truth (reducer still needs it to check the win condition).
- Client state drops `manifest` down to just `manifestSize: number` (how many items to find) + `manifestFound: string[]` (ids of items the player has actually discovered — safe to expose, they're already in `found`).
- Everywhere the client previously read `state.manifest.length`, read `state.manifestSize`.
- Everywhere the client rendered unfound manifest slots as `?` placeholders (ManifestGrid), that already works from count alone — just needs the array shape change.
- The dealer partner-bias (`manifestPartnerBias > 0`) uses manifest ids to boost tiles that are direct partners of unfound items. That's a client-side dealer call. Options:
  (a) Keep manifest ids client-side for the dealer and accept the leak, or
  (b) Move manifest-aware dealing to the server (big refactor, server has to mint trays), or
  (c) Compute the partner set server-side once and ship only the *partner ids* (a derived allowlist that doesn't reveal the manifest itself), refresh on each discovery.
  Option (c) is the sweet spot: small payload, keeps manifest hidden, dealer still gets bias signal. Partner set can leak in a limited way (the superset of recipes) but doesn't reveal which specific items are on the list.
- Server-side win check already uses `state.manifest`; unchanged.
- ENGINE_VERSION: this changes state shape, which changes storage shape and replay shape. Needs a bump + a storage hydration path for old saves (coerce `manifest: string[] | null` → `manifestSize: number`).

Scope touchpoints (grep from the earlier audit):
- `src/combine/engine.ts` — split state shape; adjust reducer to only consume `manifestSize` + `manifestFound` on the client path.
- `src/combine/storage.ts` — hydrate pre-fix saves, strip manifest ids from persisted state.
- `src/combine/server-engine.ts` — keep manifest server-side; project to client-safe shape on wire.
- `src/app/api/combine/runs/start/route.ts` + `/checkpoint` — project server state to client state before returning.
- `src/components/combine/CombineBoard.tsx` — drop `dailyManifest` prop (now unsafe); keep `dailyManifestPartnerBias`; add new partner-ids prop if going with option (c).
- `src/components/combine/CombinePageBody.tsx` — stop threading manifest ids; thread count + partner allowlist instead.
- `src/components/combine/board-parts/overlays/JourneySheet.tsx` + `ManifestGrid.tsx` — render from count, not ids, for unfound slots.
- `src/combine/deal.ts` — switch partner-bias source from `manifest` ids → partner id set.
- Tests under `src/combine/__tests__/`.

Depends on T-0254 (manifest plumbing) landing first — this is the correction to that plumbing's trust boundary.

title: security(combine): close daily puzzle information leaks to the client
body:
Umbrella for the daily-puzzle client-exposure leaks surfaced while debugging T-0254 / T-0255. The architecture ships the full engine `GameState` to the browser so the client reducer can run optimistically and the server can re-run the identical pure reducer on checkpoint. That gift has a cost: every field in state is readable from devtools, including pieces that fundamentally shouldn't be — most importantly today's daily win list.

Violates CLAUDE.md's rule: *"Daily answers stay on the server. Every move is checked server-side; the answer path is never sent to the client."*

**Threat model.** A player with devtools can:
1. Open `state.manifest` → read today's full find-list → look up recipes for each id → pre-plan the optimal path. (Primary leak, direct answer.)
2. Open `state.rng.rs` → simulate every future tray deterministically. (Secondary leak; strategic advantage, not an answer.)
3. Inspect the serialised `bundle.recipes` → know every possible recipe in play today. (Pre-existing; needed for the dealer to run.)
4. Replay/forge actions against the local reducer to lock in a score the server would reject on checkpoint drift — mitigated by server authority, but stuttering UI if abused.

The invariant that makes this hard: the client and server must run the *same* reducer with the *same* inputs, or every checkpoint 409s. Hiding manifest ids means either (a) deriving a client-safe proxy that yields identical dealer output (partner set), or (b) server-authoritative dealing (big rewrite).

**Umbrella scope.** Subtasks address each leak class separately so we can land them incrementally without destabilising the engine invariant. Order matters: T-0258 first (sets the projection pattern), then the rest can parallelise.

This is a P0 because the leak is live, the daily leaderboard is a growing visibility surface, and the fix touches the server trust boundary — the longer we wait, the more player state exists that we have to rewrite forward.

title: security(combine): introduce a client-safe GameState projection + wire protocol boundary
body:
Foundation task — the pattern every other subtask builds on. Introduce a split between `ServerGameState` (what the engine/reducer and the DB row operate on, with all authoritative fields) and `ClientGameState` (what crosses the wire and lives in the browser). Add a `projectForClient(state: ServerGameState): ClientGameState` function that is the only path server→client state can travel.

Scope:
- `src/combine/engine.ts` — rename current `GameState` to `ServerGameState` (or keep `GameState` as the server type if preferred). Define `ClientGameState` as a structural subset — initially identical so nothing breaks, then subtasks strip fields.
- Add `projectForClient()` with a strict return type. Default behaviour: deep-copy + pass through. Each subsequent subtask changes exactly one field's projection.
- `src/app/api/combine/runs/start/route.ts`, `src/app/api/combine/runs/[id]/checkpoint/route.ts`, `src/app/api/combine/runs/[id]/finish/route.ts` — every response that currently returns `state: row.stateJson` runs it through `projectForClient()` first.
- `src/combine/useCombineRun.ts` + reconcile event — accept `ClientGameState`, type-propagate.
- `src/components/combine/CombineBoard.tsx` + everywhere the client references state fields — retype to `ClientGameState`. Compile errors mark the audit surface.
- `src/combine/storage.ts` — `StoredGame` is already a client-side projection; align its shape with `ClientGameState` so hydrate→reducer→persist is a closed loop.
- Keep ENGINE_VERSION unchanged on this task; no reducer-visible behaviour changes yet.

Acceptance: `npm run typecheck` + `npm test` clean after the rename; no runtime behaviour change; subtasks T-0259 onward can pattern-match on `projectForClient` as the chokepoint.

title: security(combine): strip daily manifest ids from client state; dealer uses server-derived partner set
body:
The headline leak. Client currently receives `state.manifest: string[]` — the full daily win list, directly solving the puzzle for anyone with devtools.

Plan:
- `ClientGameState.manifest` disappears. Replace with:
  - `manifestSize: number` — for UI counts ("1 of 8 found").
  - `manifestFound: string[]` — already client-safe (ids the player has actually discovered; they're in `found` too).
  - `manifestPartnerSet: string[]` — ids that are direct recipe-partners of unfound manifest items. Derived server-side via `manifestPartnerSet(view)` from `src/combine/deal.ts:98`. Refreshed on every projection: when the player discovers a manifest item, that item's partners drop out of the set.
- `src/combine/deal.ts:pickWeighted` + `manifestPartnerSet` — the dealer currently derives `_manifestPartnerSet` lazily from `view.manifest`. Switch to reading `view.manifestPartnerSet` directly. The derivation moves to the server-side projection.
- `src/combine/engine.ts` reducer — when a manifest item is discovered, server reducer updates `state.manifest` + `state.manifestFound` + re-derives the partner set for the next projection. Client reducer only updates `manifestFound`; the next server response ships the updated partner set.
- **Dealer determinism concern:** the dealer runs on both sides. If the client's `manifestPartnerSet` ever lags the server's by one tick (e.g. the client applies a discovery locally before the server reconciles), the next optimistic tray will differ from the server's replay and 409. Mitigation: `manifestPartnerSet` is derived from `(manifest, manifestFound)` — both known at the time the reducer runs. Have `projectForClient` include the *next-tick* partner set computed assuming the pending discovery applies. Or: re-derive the partner set client-side by iterating recipes the client already has, filtered by a server-provided unfound-count — but that requires exposing which recipes matter, which re-opens the leak. Safer: ship partner set on every checkpoint response, treat optimistic dealer picks as speculative and let the reconciler correct.
- **Leak surface of the partner set itself:** an attacker can enumerate recipe outputs whose ingredients are all in the partner set — yields a *superset* of the manifest. For an 8-item manifest in a 400-recipe bundle this superset is likely 40-100 outputs, not a direct answer. Document this tradeoff in a comment next to `projectForClient`.
- `src/components/combine/board-parts/ManifestGrid.tsx` + `overlays/JourneySheet.tsx` — render unfound slots as `?` placeholders from `manifestSize - manifestFound.length` (grid already does this; just needs the shape change).
- `src/components/combine/CombineBoard.tsx` + `CombinePageBody.tsx` — remove the `dailyManifest` prop plumbing landed in T-0254. The initial manifest-aware state now comes entirely from the server's `/runs/start` response. Keep `dailyManifestPartnerBias` (it's a scalar config, not a secret).
- `src/combine/storage.ts` — pre-fix saves still have `manifest: string[]`; hydrate strips it to `manifestSize`. ENGINE_VERSION bump: the dealer's input shape changed, which is a scoring-affecting change. Bump + reject old-version replays.
- Tests: update `src/combine/__tests__/deal.test.ts` manifest-partner-bias tests to pass `manifestPartnerSet` directly.

title: security(combine): decide + act on RNG seed exposure in daily runs
body:
Secondary leak: `state.rng.rs` is shipped to the client. The client needs an RNG to run the dealer optimistically; the server needs the same seed to replay deterministically. So the seed cannot simply be hidden — the question is whether a motivated player can use it to pre-plan tray sequences and whether that matters.

Threat: knowing `rng.rs` lets an attacker fork a local copy of the engine, simulate the next N trays, and pre-plan optimal placements before seeing them. Not an answer to the puzzle, but a meaningful strategic advantage. Combined with recipe knowledge (bundle is public), a scripted player could run a solver.

Options:
1. **Accept the leak.** The dealer runs on both sides by design (CLAUDE.md invariant: "same code, same inputs"). Document the tradeoff in `GameState.rng`. Mitigate downstream with server-side anti-cheat on completion time.
2. **Server-authoritative dealing.** Server mints trays; client receives them in checkpoint responses. Rewrite of the tick loop (~a week). Removes the leak entirely but adds latency per `dealTray` call.
3. **Per-move seed advancement.** Server mints a fresh small nonce per `place` action and ships it with the response; client uses that nonce + its own local salt as the RNG input. Pre-planning only works one move ahead. Cheaper than option 2 but still a reducer rework.

Research + decision subtask (not an implementation subtask yet):
- Benchmark: how fast can a solver enumerate future trays from the current seed? If it's <1s on a laptop, this is a real cheat vector. If it's minutes, it's theoretical.
- Check whether `Shuffle for me` or `Clear` actions perturb RNG state in ways that a predictor would have to re-anchor — if they do, pre-planning is already fragile.
- Decide which option to take. If option 2 or 3, file a follow-up implementation subtask under T-0257.

Deliverable: a short writeup in task comments + a decision. Code changes only if option 1 (one comment), else a follow-up task.

title: security(combine): audit remaining ClientGameState fields for leak surface
body:
Once T-0258 lands and `ClientGameState` is a named type, walk every field and classify it: `safe` (render-only, no advantage), `derived-leak` (reveals info beyond what the UI shows), or `authoritative-only` (should never leave the server). Covers fields not already addressed in T-0259 (manifest) and T-0260 (rng).

Fields to classify (from `GameState` in `src/combine/engine.ts:120-230`):
- `howMade: Record<string, Signature[]>` — records which exact recipes produced each discovered item. Could leak optimal recipe hints for items the player hasn't tried yet (if the server pre-fills it).
- `discoveredAtChapter: Record<string, number>` — per-item chapter attribution. Likely safe (it's derived from the player's own history).
- `madeCounts: Record<string, number>` — per-item make tallies. Safe (player's own history).
- `closeCalls: number` — count of near-crumble saves. Safe.
- `recentTrays: string[][]` — anti-repetition memory. Already in the state; combined with rng gives a one-tick prediction. Safe-ish, but if RNG gets hidden in T-0260 this needs re-review.
- `lastSnapshot` — undo backup. Safe (it's the player's own prior state).
- `initialSeed: number | null` — daily payload seed. Needed client-side for the stale-save guard; already public via DailyPayload. Safe.
- `shored: boolean[]` — crumble-timer suppression per cell. Safe.
- `crumb: (Crumb | null)[]` — per-cell crumble state. Safe.
- `scripted` (tutorial-only) — scripted dealer queue. Safe (tutorial has no competitive stakes).
- `choosing` — pending recipe-pick UI state. Safe.

Also audit the `bundle` serialisation separately: `bundle.recipes` is already fully public and likely has to stay that way (the dealer needs it), but confirm there's nothing else in the bundle that shouldn't be (e.g. private theme notes, draft recipes).

Deliverable: a classification table in task comments. Any `derived-leak` fields get a follow-up implementation subtask filed under T-0257.

title: security(combine): server-side anti-cheat on daily completion (time/action-count floors)
body:
Defence-in-depth layer. Even with manifest + RNG hidden, a sufficiently motivated attacker can reverse-engineer the client, forge a server-signed action sequence, or just automate play faster than any human. For the leaderboard to mean anything, the server needs to reject obviously-impossible completions at the `/runs/:id/finish` boundary.

Scope:
- Measure realistic completion floors from current legitimate top scores. Expected shape: minimum N moves >= manifest size (can't win with fewer moves than items), minimum wall-clock time between `startedAt` and `finishedAt` (e.g. median move interval × manifest size), maximum actions-per-second (a human can't click faster than ~5/s sustained).
- `src/app/api/combine/runs/[id]/finish/route.ts` — add floor checks. On violation: reject the finish (don't record the result), log to a server-side cheat-audit table, and return a 422 with a vague "run invalidated" message (don't tip off the attacker which check tripped).
- Decide whether to also strip the affected `progress` row from the leaderboard query (preferred: never insert it) vs. a nightly cleanup job.
- Admin surface: a page under `/admin/combine` listing recent audit hits so we can calibrate the floors over time without blocking legitimate players.

Deliberately filed separate from the hide-the-state subtasks because this works even if the state hiding is incomplete — it's a different layer of the same defence.

title: security(combine): tighten start-daily auth — require markStartedDaily before any manifest-bearing state ships
body:
T-0247 added `markStartedDaily` to stamp a server-side start time so reload can't "peek" at the daily and restart the clock. Related concern: even with manifest ids hidden (T-0259), the partner set + chapter progression hints are still exposed from the moment `runs/start` is called — which happens before the Start-daily sheet is confirmed.

Scope:
- Audit `/api/combine/runs/start` for daily mode: does it currently require the player to have confirmed Start, or does it mint a run + ship state on first page load?
- If it ships state pre-confirm, change the flow: `runs/start` for daily returns only a run id + bundle info, no manifest-bearing state. Call `runs/:id/materialize` (new endpoint) after confirm to ship the stateful bits.
- Trade-off: this adds a round-trip to the Start-daily flow. Acceptable because it's a one-time per-day cost at the natural pause point.
- Reconcile with the T-0254 fix (manifest comes from server now, no longer from the page-body prop) — the materialize endpoint becomes the single source.

Lower priority than T-0259/T-0260 because the leak window is "page loaded but Start not clicked" (small in practice), but worth cleaning up for symmetry with the server-start clock.

title: feat(combine): rework daily Journey manifest UI to row list w/ turns-ago
body:
## Scope

Replace the `ManifestGrid` inside the `DailyJourney` branch of `JourneySheet.tsx` with a vertical row list. Each row: `[icon · name · found indicator · turns-ago]`.

Start-daily sheet (CombineBoard) and GameOverCard continue to use `ManifestGrid` — they are pre-run previews / post-run summaries where the compact grid works better.

## Design

- Row anatomy (left → right):
  - 28px tier-filled icon tile (Pictogram)
  - Name (ellipsis on overflow)
  - Found/to-find indicator (✓ chip or `· to find` text)
  - Trailing meta: `3 turns ago` for found; blank for unfound

- "Turns ago" is derived client-side only: watch `state.manifestFound` for new ids and record the `state.moves` value at that moment into a `useRef<Map<string, number>>`. Clears on `manifest` change (daily rollover / new run).

- No `GameState` change, no `ENGINE_VERSION` bump — cosmetic.

## Files

- `src/components/combine/board-parts/overlays/JourneySheet.tsx` — new `ManifestRowList` subcomponent
- `src/app/globals.css` — add row styles (`.cbmanifest-row`, etc.)

## Why

Icon-only grid in the in-run sheet is hard to scan when the manifest grows past ~10. Names + turn-attribution give the player a sense of pacing within the daily (which is scored on turns). Start sheet and GameOver keep the grid because they favour spatial scan.

## Out of scope

- Any engine/server state change.
- Changing `ManifestGrid` itself.
- "Minutes ago" wall-clock — turns track the scoring axis and don't drift on pause/resume.

comments.body:
## Approach

Keep `ManifestGrid` untouched (start-sheet + GameOver still use it). Add a new `ManifestRowList` subcomponent inside `JourneySheet.tsx` — scoped there since turns-ago tracking is journey-specific (client-only state).

**Turns-ago attribution:**
- `useRef<Map<string, number>>` keyed by manifest item id → `state.moves` at discovery time.
- `useEffect` on `[state.manifestFound]`: for each id in `manifestFound` not in the ref, set ref.current.set(id, state.moves). Items already in ref keep their original move stamp (don't overwrite).
- `useEffect` on `[manifest.join(",")]`: clear the ref when manifest identity changes (new daily / new run).
- Render: `delta = state.moves - foundAt`; show `found` (just ✓) when delta == 0, else `Nt ago` (compact; `t` = turn).

**Row layout (CSS grid: 32px 1fr auto):**
- Left: icon tile — reuse `cbmanifest-tile` mini (36→32px), tier fill. Drop stacked-text since row already has a name slot.
- Middle: name (bold, ellipsis).
- Right: meta — found rows show `✓ 3t ago` in mono; unfound rows show `to find` in muted mono.

**Found rows dim** to match grid semantics (opacity .55, like `.cbmanifest-tile-found`), unfound stay vivid.

**Order:** manifest order (same as grid) — not find order, because the player's mental model of the list is stable and found items dim out of focus.

CSS: add `.cbmanifest-rows`, `.cbmanifest-row`, `.cbmanifest-row-ic`, `.cbmanifest-row-name`, `.cbmanifest-row-meta`, `.cbmanifest-row.found` to `globals.css` beside existing manifest styles.

## Landed

**Files touched:**
- `src/components/combine/board-parts/overlays/JourneySheet.tsx:1,10` — dropped `ManifestGrid` import; added `useEffect`, `useRef` imports.
- `src/components/combine/board-parts/overlays/JourneySheet.tsx:78-84` — swapped `<ManifestGrid …/>` for `<ManifestRowList …/>` in `DailyJourney`.
- `src/components/combine/board-parts/overlays/JourneySheet.tsx:260-340` — new `ManifestRowList` subcomponent (ref-based turns-ago attribution, resets on manifest identity change).
- `src/app/globals.css:1714-1729` — added `.cbmanifest-rows` / `.cbmanifest-row-*` styles.

**Validation:**
- `npm run typecheck` ✓ clean.
- `npm run lint` ✓ no new warnings in touched files.
- `npm test` ✓ 477 passed / 11 skipped.
- Visual check pending — user confirmed lgtm.

**Notes:**
- `ManifestGrid` retained unchanged (start-sheet + GameOverCard still use it).
- Turns-ago is client-only; nothing persisted, no `ENGINE_VERSION` bump.
- `foundAt` for items already in `manifestFound` when the journey first renders stamps as "0t ago / just now" rather than the true discovery turn — acceptable because the ref is populated lazily, and the "just now" fallback reads cleanly. Full accuracy would need `GameState.manifestFoundAt` (engine change).

title: feat(combine): ChapterBar shows manifest progress in daily mode
body:
## Problem

`ChapterBar.tsx` always renders chapter progression ("Ch N — X/Y → N+1"), even in daily mode. Daily is manifest-driven — chapter thresholds are irrelevant to that run's goal. The T-0240 comment in the file already flags this as a pending T-0244 cleanup.

## Fix

In daily mode (`state.mode === "daily"` and `state.manifest?.length > 0`), render:
- bar fill = `manifestFound.length / manifest.length`
- left label: `Daily`
- right label: `${foundCount}/${total} manifest` (or at 100%: `Complete`)
- aria mirrors the same wording

Endless/fast behaviour unchanged.

## Files

- `src/components/combine/board-parts/board/ChapterBar.tsx`

## Notes

- Tapping the bar still routes `onAges` → JourneySheet; the daily branch of JourneySheet already shows manifest rows, so the handoff is coherent.
- When daily has no manifest (legacy daily, `manifest=null`), fall back to chapter progression — same path as today.

comments.body:
## Landed

**Files touched:**
- `src/components/combine/board-parts/board/ChapterBar.tsx:6-48` — gated on `state.mode === "daily"` + non-empty `state.manifest`; renders `Daily — X/Y manifest` bar when daily-with-manifest, falls through to chapter progression otherwise (endless / fast / legacy-daily-with-null-manifest).

**Validation:**
- `npm run typecheck` ✓ clean.
- No tests cover ChapterBar directly; visual verification needed.

**Behaviour:**
- Daily (manifest 0/8) → "Daily · 0/8 manifest", bar empty.
- Daily (manifest 5/8) → "Daily · 5/8 manifest", bar 63%.
- Daily complete (8/8) → "Daily · Complete", bar full.
- Endless/fast/legacy-daily → unchanged.

title: Daily 'Ready?' sheet traps user — can't reach TopBar menu to leave
body:
When the Daily `dailyStartPending` ResponsiveSheet opens in CombineBoard.tsx:2579, its full-viewport scrim (z-index 300) covers the TopBar. Because the sheet uses `dismissOnScrim={false}` with no other close affordance besides "Start", the player is forced to start the daily — they can't open More, switch theme, or go home.

Fix: give the sheet a close/back affordance (the daily commitment gate shouldn't become a jail). Simplest option: add a close "X" button on the sheet that reverts `dailyStartPending` so the user falls back to the normal board (or theme picker). The commitment gate (no scrim-dismiss, no Esc) stays in place for accidental taps.

comments.body:
Approach: user suggested adding a "Not ready" button inside the dialog rather than changing TopBar visibility — cleaner since the scrim commitment gate stays intact for stray-tap protection.

Plan:
- Add a `preDailyStateRef` captured in `startDaily()` before the setState to daily (so we can restore to the exact pre-daily state without re-deriving mode/theme/save slot).
- Add `cancelStartDaily` callback: restores `preDailyStateRef.current`, clears `dailyStartPending`, resets daily timer refs.
- Add a "Not ready" secondary button in the ResponsiveSheet alongside "Start" — wired through ButtonGroup.

Files: `src/components/combine/CombineBoard.tsx` only. No DB / engine / API changes, no ENGINE_VERSION bump.

Landed in `src/components/combine/CombineBoard.tsx`:

- `cancelStartDaily` callback (CombineBoard.tsx:1532-1557): flips `dailyStartPending` off, clears daily timer refs, then mirrors the mount-time fallback ladder — fast save for `activeTheme` → endless save for `activeTheme` → fresh endless. Chosen over snapshotting the pre-daily state because the prior game could be yesterday's daily; restoring it would strand the player on a stale daily whose server slot doesn't match today.
- "Not ready" button added alongside "Start" in the ResponsiveSheet (CombineBoard.tsx:2628-2635).

Deliberately did NOT re-enable scrim/Esc dismiss on the sheet — the commitment gate still blocks stray clicks, now with an explicit exit label instead.

`npm run typecheck` clean. Not manually tested in browser.

title: fix(combine): shimmer placeholder missing helpers container next to hold
body:
`BoardPlaceholder` renders `.cbholdrow` with only the `.cbhold` shelf inside. The live Hold renders `.cbhold` AND a sibling `.cbhelpwrap` (HelpersButton). Since `.cbholdrow` is a flex row with `.cbhold { flex:1 1 auto }` and `.cbhelpwrap { flex:0 0 auto }`, the skeleton's hold stretches full-width and the real board snaps leftward when it mounts — visible layout mismatch during the shimmer → live swap.

Fix: add a `.cbhelpwrap` placeholder sibling inside the skeleton's `cbholdrow` that reserves roughly the HelpersButton's footprint.

comments.body:
Approach: edit `src/components/combine/board-parts/board/BoardPlaceholder.tsx` to add a `.cbhelpwrap` sibling next to `.cbhold` inside the `cbholdrow`, containing a shimmer stand-in button with the same `.cbh.cbhelpbtn` footprint as HelpersButton (so flex sizing matches). No CSS changes needed — existing `.cbholdrow > .cbhelpwrap` rules already constrain width; adding `cb-skel-tile` style would be overkill. Instead render a muted placeholder that borrows the shimmer treatment via a new small rule, or reuse an existing shimmer class. Will apply the shimmer effect using the existing `::after` keyframe by tagging the inner span with a skeleton class. Minimal: one element, no new CSS rule needed if we use `cb-skel-slot` styling at the right width — but width is dictated by `.cbh.cbhelpbtn`. Simplest: render `
` with a tiny CSS rule giving `.cb-skel-help` fixed min-width matching the real button text. Let me measure vs. just making the stand-in also stretch to match.

Landed:
- `src/components/combine/board-parts/board/BoardPlaceholder.tsx`: added `.cbhelpwrap` sibling inside `.cbholdrow` holding a `<span class="cbh cbhelpbtn cb-skel-helpbtn">` with the same SVG + "Helpers" label + count slot the live button uses, so flex sizing is identical.
- `src/app/globals.css` (after line 1105): new `.cb-skel-helpbtn` rule giving a muted color/border/background + shimmer `::after` matching the rest of the skeleton palette. Reduced-motion rule extended to include it.

Verified `.cbholdrow > .cbhelpwrap { flex:0 0 auto }` already constrains width (globals.css:968) so the stand-in snaps to real-button width automatically. `npm run typecheck` passes.
